info.title: Criptonlabs Agent APIs
info.description: Agent-native, read-only XRP Ledger and Solana APIs. Errors are RFC 9457 problem+json.
info.x-guidance: Read-only XRPL data. Free /v1/* routes and /mcp need no key or payment; start at /llms.txt. Check /v1/xrpl/fee, /v1/xrpl/network/health and /v1/xrpl/account/{address}/summary before building a transaction. Read meta.stale and meta.age_seconds on every response. /v1/pro/* and /mcp/pro are paid per call via x402 in USDC or EURC on Solana or RLUSD on XRPL (XRP and other currencies refused), VAT included; see https://api.criptonlabs.com/v1/pro/requirements and /docs/pro.md.

invalid-parameters.retry: No. The same request fails again.
invalid-parameters.recovery: Correct the listed fields (positive decimal `amount`, `depth` a positive integer (rounded up to 10, 50 or 100), valid `window`) and call again. Currency and asset format: `XRP`, or `CODE.issuer`: `CODE` is a 3-character standard code or 40 hexadecimal digits, and `issuer` is a classic XRPL address. Standard codes are case-sensitive: `usd` and `USD` are different tokens, so send the exact code. A standard code uses letters, digits or `?!@#$%^&*<>(){}[]|` and is never `XRP`; percent-encode the symbols in a URL (for example `%3F` for `?`). A 40-hex code is read in any case, and the 40-hex form of a standard code means that code. For header and credential fields, send one valid `Idempotency-Key` header, one `Authorization: Bearer` token, and a SIWX proof in only one place: either `_meta` or the `SIGN-IN-WITH-X` header, never both.

bad-request.retry: No. Client errors from the upstream node are not retried.
bad-request.recovery: Check the parameters against the endpoint page; the `upstream_code` member names the upstream error code.

not-found.retry: No, unless the object may be created later (for example a new account is funded).
not-found.recovery: Verify the address or currency pair. A missing AMM pool is a normal answer, not an outage.

solana-mint-not-found.retry: No, unless the mint may be created later.
solana-mint-not-found.recovery: Check the mint address (not a wallet or a token account) and that it exists on Solana. For native SOL use `mint=SOL` on transfer readiness.

method-not-allowed.retry: No. Repeat the call with GET.
method-not-allowed.recovery: Use GET on the exact path; the `Allow` header lists the accepted method.

rate-limited.retry: Yes, after the delay in the `Retry-After` header (also `retry_after_seconds` in the body). For the daily free quota the delay runs to the next 00:00 UTC.
rate-limited.recovery: Wait for the delay, slow down, and reuse cached answers: data is fresh for only a few seconds, so polling faster than the TTL gains nothing. A 429 whose body is the plain text `error code: 1015` comes from the burst limit in front of the service and has no problem body; honor its `Retry-After` the same way.

internal-error.retry: Yes, a few times with backoff. If it persists, stop and report it.
internal-error.recovery: There is nothing to fix in the request.

upstream-unavailable.retry: Yes, after the `Retry-After` delay (5 seconds, also `retry_after_seconds` in the body).
upstream-unavailable.recovery: Retry with backoff. Check `/v1/xrpl/network/health` or `/v1/solana/health` for the state of the upstream nodes.

payment-required.retry: Yes, with a valid payment: sign a payment for one of the listed options and repeat the request with it in the `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` header.
payment-required.recovery: Read `accepts` from the `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` header (or `GET /v1/pro/requirements`), sign a payment for exactly that amount, asset, network and resource, and send it with the request. The free routes under `/v1/` need no payment. When the body carries an `error` member naming a credit refusal reason, read the section of that reason below.

payments-unavailable.retry: Yes, later with backoff, with a new payment: the earlier one was released and cannot be used again.
payments-unavailable.recovery: Retry after a short delay, or use the free routes under `/v1/`, which serve the same data without payment.

payment-settlement-failed.retry: Yes, with a new payment: sign again and repeat the request.
payment-settlement-failed.recovery: Sign a new payment and resend. If your wallet was debited without a response, keep the transaction signature and check it on the network before paying again. For a top-up with a `pending_token`, try the token later instead of paying again: until the payment is reconciled it is refused with `credits_invalid`. On the XRP Ledger, repeating the top-up with the same signed transaction answers 201 once the payment is reconciled; the body states that the earlier `pending_token` is now valid, carries no new token and no balance (the balance comes back in `X-Credits-Remaining` on a call made with the token).

payment-already-used.recovery: Always sign a new payment for every new call; resend a payment only for the same request, within 5 minutes and at most 3 times.

payer-blocked.recovery: Use a different payer wallet, or the free routes under `/v1/`, which need no payment.

payer-limit-reached.retry: Yes, after the time in the `Retry-After` header (seconds until 00:00 UTC, also `retry_after_seconds` in the body).
payer-limit-reached.recovery: Wait for the delay. Check that the payer wallet holds enough balance and that payments are signed correctly to avoid failed settlements.

idempotency-key-conflict.retry: No, not with the same key.
idempotency-key-conflict.recovery: Send the request again with a new idempotency key.

payment-attempts-limited.retry: Yes, after the delay in the `Retry-After` header (seconds until the lock ends, also `retry_after_seconds` in the body).
payment-attempts-limited.recovery: Wait for the delay and check the payment (amount, asset, network, resource and signature) before signing it again. To check the offer meanwhile, repeat the call without a payment or use `GET /v1/pro/requirements`.

payment-in-progress.retry: Yes. `Retry-After` (also `retry_after_seconds` in the body) gives the seconds to wait; send the same request with the same payment again after that time.
payment-in-progress.recovery: Send the same request with the same payment again after the `Retry-After` time, and sign no new payment for it.

docs.description: Documentation page of the route or tool.

score.description: Integer from 0 to 100, the project composite: 0.5 x queue fill (current_queue_size / max_queue_size) + 0.3 x open-ledger fee pressure + 0.2 x load factor pressure; the queue term is 0 when rippled reports no max_queue_size

band.description: Band of the composite score: low below 30, medium below 70, high from 70

load_factor_multiplier.description: The server load factor the score used, decimal string; null when load_factor_assumed is true

escalation_multiplier.description: The open-ledger cost as a multiple of the reference cost, a factor: rippled `fee` levels.open_ledger_level / levels.reference_level, decimal string. It is not rippled's escalationMultiplier, which is the median fee level

base_fee_drops.description: Reference transaction cost, a decimal string in drops (rippled `fee` drops.base_fee)

median_fee_drops.description: rippled's escalation multiplier in drops: the median fee level of the last closed ledger, floored at the minimum; it sets no tier

minimum_fee_drops.description: Lowest cost that enters the queue now, a decimal string in drops (rippled `fee` drops.minimum_fee)

open_ledger_fee_drops.description: Lowest cost that enters the open ledger now, a decimal string in drops (rippled `fee` drops.open_ledger_fee)

max_queue_size.description: Most transactions the queue can hold (rippled `fee` max_queue_size), a JSON integer; null when rippled reports no queue maximum

current_ledger_size.description: Transactions in the current open ledger (rippled current_ledger_size)

expected_ledger_size.description: Transactions rippled expects in the current ledger (rippled expected_ledger_size)

ledger_fill_ratio.description: Open ledger fill, a fraction: current_ledger_size / expected_ledger_size (rippled `fee`), decimal string; null when expected_ledger_size is 0

ledger_index.description: Ledger the data comes from; ledger_state says whether it is validated or open

ledger_state.description: State of the ledger ledger_index names: open for the fee read, which reads the open ledger, else validated; a composite answer is open only when every read is

as_of.description: When we read the data from the ledger (our read time), not the ledger close time

age_seconds.description: Age of our read at response time, not of the ledger close time

cache.description: Cache state; a composite answer reports the worst state of its reads, miss above stale

stale.description: True when served past its fresh TTL (stale-on-error)

ledger_age_seconds.description: Age of the node's latest validated ledger at the last probe, in seconds: server_info's validated_ledger.age. rippled reports 0 once the age reaches 1,000,000 s, so 0 alone does not prove a fresh ledger. Null when the node was down at the last probe or reported no age

load_factor_multiplier.description: The node's server load factor without open-ledger fee escalation, decimal string: server_info's load_factor_server (its load_factor when the node omits it) at the last probe; 1 means no load. Null when the last probe reported none.

server_state.description: The node's server_info server_state at the last probe: whether it follows the network now. full has the ledger and agrees with the network; tracking, syncing, connected and disconnected lag or are not in sync. Null when the node did not answer, the value was not stored yet, or it is outside these five.

complete_ledgers.description: The node's server_info complete_ledgers at the last probe, parsed into ranges in rippled's order, both bounds included (a single ledger has equal bounds): which ledgers the node can answer, for transactions paging and past-ledger reads. [] when the node holds none (rippled's empty). Null when the node did not answer, the value was not stored yet, or it does not parse as rippled's format.

amendment_blocked.description: The node's server_info amendment_blocked at the last probe: true when the node has stopped following the network until it is upgraded; false when server_info omits it (rippled writes it only when blocked). Null when the node did not answer or the value was not stored yet.

error.description: The node's last probe error as a code matching ^[A-Za-z0-9_]{1,40}$, such as timeout or http_503; any other upstream error text is reported as upstream_error. Null when the last probe succeeded.

median_latency_ms.description: The median latency_ms of the up nodes' latest samples (the mean of the two middle values for an even count); null when no node is up

ledger_index.description: Ledger the data comes from; ledger_state says whether it is validated or open; null when no read behind the answer names a ledger, never 0

ledger_state.description: State of the ledger ledger_index names: open for the fee read, which reads the open ledger, else validated; a composite answer is open only when every read is

as_of.description: When we read the data from the ledger (our read time), not the ledger close time

age_seconds.description: Age of our read at response time, not of the ledger close time

cache.description: Cache state; a composite answer reports the worst state of its reads, miss above stale

stale.description: True when served past its fresh TTL (stale-on-error)

uptime_pct.description: The member's up / samples x 100 in this bucket, in percent, a decimal string rounded half-up to 2 places; it counts probe samples, not elapsed time

member.description: The node, under the name the buckets and the summary use

uptime_pct.description: The node's up samples / its samples x 100 over the whole window, in percent, a decimal string rounded half-up to 2 places; it counts probe samples, not elapsed time

median_latency_ms.description: The median latency_ms of the node's up samples over the window (the mean of the two middle values for an even count); null with no up sample

nodes.description: One entry per node over the whole window, sorted by member

close_age_seconds.description: Whole seconds from close_time to the response time, never below 0; null when close_time is null

base.description: Base asset queried, in the canonical form the route reads (echo)

base_currency_ascii.description: Readable text of `base`'s 40-hex currency code; null when not printable ASCII; absent for XRP and 3-character codes

quote.description: Quote asset queried, in the canonical form the route reads (echo)

quote_currency_ascii.description: Readable text of `quote`'s 40-hex currency code; null when not printable ASCII; absent for XRP and 3-character codes

domain.description: PermissionedDomain id queried, upper-case hex (echo of `domain`); null when the request sent none (the open book)

depth.description: The requested depth, echoed; 10, the default, when the request names none

depth_effective.description: Depth bucket served: the requested depth rounded up to 10, 50 or 100, at most 100. Each side lists at most this many levels

asks_truncated.description: True when the ask side's `book_offers` page returned as many offers as the depth bucket, counted before zero-amount offers are skipped

bids_truncated.description: True when the bid side's `book_offers` page returned as many offers as the depth bucket, counted before zero-amount offers are skipped

best_bid.description: Highest bid price, quote per base; null when there are no bids or the best bid is zero

best_ask.description: Lowest ask price, quote per base; null when there are no asks or the best ask is zero

mid.description: Midpoint of best_bid and best_ask, quote per base; null when a side is empty or its best price is zero

spread_price.description: best_ask minus best_bid, quote per base (negative when crossed); null when a side is empty or its best price is zero

spread_bps.description: spread_price / mid x 10,000, in basis points, rounded half-up to 2 decimals; null when a side is empty or its best price is zero

crossed.description: True when best_bid is above best_ask; null when a side is empty or its best price is zero

ask_depth.description: Funded ask quantity of the levels read, a decimal string in units of `base`

bid_depth.description: Funded bid quantity of the levels read, a decimal string in units of `base`

funded_total.description: Per side: total funded base quantity of the levels read

half_width_bps.description: Band half-width around mid, in basis points: 10, 50 or 100

ask_depth.description: Funded ask quantity within the band, a decimal string in units of `base`

bid_depth.description: Funded bid quantity within the band, a decimal string in units of `base`

depth_bands.description: Funded base quantity per side within 10, 50 and 100 bps of mid, bounds included; null when a side is empty or its best price is zero

asks.description: One level per funded offer, in book order, best (lowest) price first, not a price aggregate; offers expired at or before the close time of the latest validated ledger are left out, possibly a few seconds early

bids.description: One level per funded offer, in book order, best (highest) price first, from the base-asset side, not a price aggregate; offers expired at or before the close time of the latest validated ledger are left out, possibly a few seconds early

gets.description: Funded base quantity of the offer, a decimal string in units of `base` (XRP in XRP, not drops), on both sides

pays.description: Funded quote quantity of the offer, a decimal string in units of `quote` (XRP in XRP, not drops), on both sides

owner.description: The account that placed the offer (its maker, the offer's Account)

expires_at.description: When the offer expires (its Expiration), RFC 3339 with milliseconds; null when it has no expiry

base.description: Base asset queried, in the canonical form the route reads (echo)

base_currency_ascii.description: Readable text of `base`'s 40-hex currency code; null when not printable ASCII; absent for XRP and 3-character codes

quote.description: Quote asset queried, in the canonical form the route reads (echo)

quote_currency_ascii.description: Readable text of `quote`'s 40-hex currency code; null when not printable ASCII; absent for XRP and 3-character codes

domain.description: PermissionedDomain id queried, upper-case hex (echo of `domain`); null when the request sent none (the open book)

side.description: buy walks the asks; sell walks the bids

depth.description: The requested depth, echoed; 100, the default, when the request names none

depth_effective.description: Depth bucket served: the requested depth rounded up to 10, 50 or 100, at most 100. The walk reads at most this many levels of the walked side

amount.description: Base quantity to buy or sell (the request's `amount`), a decimal string in units of `base`

filled.description: Base quantity the walk fills, at most `amount`, a decimal string in units of `base`

partial.description: True when filled is above 0 and below amount; the top-level prices then describe the filled part

book_truncated.description: True when liquidity is insufficient and the server returned as many offers for the walked side as the read requested, the depth bucket served, so the book may hold more than was read

best_price.description: Price of the best level of the walked side (best ask on a buy, best bid on a sell), a decimal string, quote per base; null when that side is empty or its best level's price is zero

worst_price.description: Price of the worst book level the reported fill reaches (the last level the walk consumes, in rippled's crossing order), quote per base; null when nothing is filled or there is no best price

avg_price.description: Average price of the filled part, a decimal string, quote per base: paid on a buy, received on a sell; null when nothing is filled or there is no best price

slippage_pct.description: Percent; on a partial fill, of the filled part; null when nothing is filled or there is no best price

transfer_fee_applied.description: True when the transfer fee of the asset the taker sends is known (its issuer's TransferRate was loaded, or the taker sends XRP, which has none), so transfer_fee_pct and avg_price_after_fees are set; false when the rate could not be loaded, and both are null. best_price, worst_price, avg_price and slippage_pct never include the transfer fee

transfer_fee_pct.description: Transfer fee of the asset the taker sends in percent, (TransferRate - 1000000000) / 10000000, exact; "0" when it sends XRP; null when the rate could not be loaded

transfer_fee_issuer.description: Issuer whose TransferRate applies: the issuer of the asset the taker sends (quote on a buy, base on a sell); null when it sends XRP or the rate could not be loaded

avg_price_after_fees.description: avg_price after the TransferRate of the asset the taker sends (x r/1e9 on a buy, / r/1e9 on a sell), a decimal string, quote per base; null when nothing is filled or the rate could not be loaded

best.description: Venue with the better avg_price for the side (lower on a buy, higher on a sell; ties go to the CLOB), null when neither can fill

amm_status.description: State of the AMM read: ok, stale (served past its fresh window), no_pool (no pool for the pair, or an empty one), frozen (a pool asset is frozen, so the pool is not used), unavailable

avg_price.description: Quote per base: paid on a buy, received on a sell; null when it cannot fill

cost.description: Total quote for `amount`, in units of `quote`: paid on a buy, received on a sell; null when it cannot fill

slippage_pct.description: Percent vs the best ask (buy) or best bid (sell), null when it cannot fill

avg_price_after_fees.description: avg_price after the TransferRate of the asset the taker sends (x r/1e9 on a buy, / r/1e9 on a sell), quote per base; null when the rate is unknown

avg_price.description: Quote per base: paid on a buy, received on a sell; null when it cannot fill

cost.description: Total quote for `amount`, in units of `quote`: paid on a buy, received on a sell; null when it cannot fill

slippage_pct.description: Percent vs the fee-free pool spot price (includes the trading fee), null when it cannot fill

avg_price_after_fees.description: avg_price after the TransferRate of the asset the taker sends (x r/1e9 on a buy, / r/1e9 on a sell), quote per base; null when the rate is unknown

spot_price.description: Pool spot price, quote per base, excluding fee and impact

spot_price_with_fee.description: Marginal pool price including the trading fee, quote per base: spot / (1 - fee) for a buy, spot x (1 - fee) for a sell, with fee = trading_fee_pct / 100

trading_fee_pct.description: Pool trading fee in percent (TradingFee / 1000, exact), like /v1/xrpl/amm

amm.description: Null when the pair has no pool, the pool is empty or frozen, or it could not be read (see amm_status)

amm_ledger_index.description: Ledger of the AMM read shown in venues.amm; null when venues.amm is null

amm_age_seconds.description: Age in seconds of the AMM read shown in venues.amm; null when venues.amm is null

venues.description: CLOB vs AMM comparison for the same amount; no routing split

asset_a_currency_ascii.description: Readable text of `asset_a`'s 40-hex currency code; null when not printable ASCII; absent for XRP and 3-character codes

asset_b_currency_ascii.description: Readable text of `asset_b`'s 40-hex currency code; null when not printable ASCII; absent for XRP and 3-character codes

reserve_a.description: Pool reserve of `asset_a`, a decimal string in units of `asset_a` (XRP in XRP, not drops)

reserve_b.description: Pool reserve of `asset_b`, a decimal string in units of `asset_b` (XRP in XRP, not drops)

trading_fee_pct.description: Pool trading fee in percent: TradingFee / 1000, exact

spot_a_per_b.description: Fee-free pool price of one b in a: reserve_a / reserve_b; null for an empty pool

spot_a_per_b_with_fee.description: Marginal price of one b in a including the trading fee: spot_a_per_b / (1 - trading_fee_pct / 100); null for an empty pool

spot_b_per_a.description: Fee-free pool price of one a in b: reserve_b / reserve_a; null for an empty pool

spot_b_per_a_with_fee.description: Marginal price of one a in b including the trading fee: spot_b_per_a / (1 - trading_fee_pct / 100); null for an empty pool

currency_ascii.description: Readable text of the LP token's 40-hex code; null when not printable ASCII (an AMM LP code starts with 0x03, so null)

supply.description: Outstanding LP tokens (LPTokenBalance), a decimal string in LP tokens

lp_token.description: LP token of the pool: currency code, issuer (the AMM account) and outstanding supply

a_per_lp_token.description: reserve_a / supply: units of asset_a per LP token; null for an empty pool

b_per_lp_token.description: reserve_b / supply: units of asset_b per LP token; null for an empty pool

account.description: Holder of the slot, who trades at the discounted fee (amm_info auction_slot.account, the slot's Account)

get.summary: Current payment options of a paid resource, or the price index, without paying.
get.description:
With `resource`, returns the `accepts` entries the paid route or tool would offer in its 402 challenge, so a client can sign a payment before the first call. Without it, returns the price index: every paid route and MCP tool with its per-call price (VAT included), network, asset and mint when paid access is active, and links to each per-resource offer and docs page; outside x402 mode it lists the resources and `payments_mode` only and names no price. Free and never challenged: it is counted in the `cheap` rate tier. In x402 mode the route answers 503 `payments-unavailable` when the x402 configuration is invalid or no facilitator can currently offer a payment; `accepts` is empty only when `payments_mode` is off or gateway (no paid access). The offer follows the facilitator set and its health, so the live source of truth is this route or the `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` header of a 402.

When to use: you want to prepay on the first call instead of paying after a 402.

When not to use: you only need data; the free routes carry the same data without payment.

schema.description: Optional. Omit it for the price index of every paid route and tool. Otherwise a `/v1/pro/*` path (or its URL) without a query string, or `mcp://criptonlabs/pro/<tool>` for a paid MCP tool. The payment you sign is bound to exactly this resource.

get.summary: Current XRPL fee tiers in drops with a congestion score.
get.description:
Returns economy, standard and priority fees in drops plus a 0-100 congestion score and band (`low`, `medium`, `high`), the project composite 0.5 x queue fill + 0.3 x open-ledger fee pressure + 0.2 x load factor pressure; the queue term is 0 when rippled reports no `max_queue_size`, and `congestion.load_factor_multiplier` is the load factor the score used (`null` when `load_factor_assumed` is `true`). `queue_full` is `true` when `minimum_fee_drops` is above `base_fee_drops`, and `escalation_multiplier` is the open-ledger cost as a multiple of the reference cost (the open-ledger fee level divided by the reference level, as a decimal string), not rippled's `escalationMultiplier`, which `median_fee_drops` gives in drops: the median fee level of the last closed ledger, floored at the minimum. `current_queue_size`, `max_queue_size` (`null` when rippled reports no queue maximum), `current_ledger_size` and `expected_ledger_size` are JSON integers, and `ledger_fill_ratio` = current_ledger_size / expected_ledger_size (`null` when the expected size is 0). Its `ledger_index` is the current open ledger, and `meta.ledger_state` is `open`.

When to use: Before submitting a transaction, to choose a `Fee` and to decide whether the network is congested.

When not to use: Not a price feed and not a historical series; it describes the current open ledger only.

get.summary: Overall and per-node health of the upstream XRPL nodes (alias of network health).
get.description:

get.summary: CLOB order book for a currency pair with unfunded offers removed.
get.description:
Returns asks (best price first) and bids as levels `{gets, pays, price, owner, expires_at}`, one level per funded offer in book order, not a price aggregate: `owner` is the account that placed the offer and `expires_at` its expiry (RFC 3339 with milliseconds, `null` when it has none). Funded amounts are used when the ledger reports them and zero-amount levels are dropped. Price is `pays` per `gets` in human units (XRP, not drops). Offers whose expiry is at or before the close time of the latest validated ledger are left out of the levels and of every statistic, since the ledger no longer crosses them; that close time can be a few seconds later than the book's ledger, so an offer may be left out slightly early. `depth` echoes the requested depth (10 when absent); it is bucketed to 10, 50 or 100 levels per side, a larger depth is served at 100, and `depth_effective` reports the bucket served. `asks_truncated` and `bids_truncated` are true when the server returned as many offers for that side as the read requested (the depth bucket served), expired offers included, so the book may hold more. Both sides are read on one validated ledger, the one `meta.ledger_index` reports; `meta` also covers the latest-ledger read that gives the close time, and when that close time cannot be read, or a page holds an offer without its `Account` (a field the ledger requires), the answer fails as a failed read does (503 `upstream-unavailable`). The statistics are computed from all levels read, with prices in quote per base and quantities in base: `best_bid`, `best_ask`, `mid`, `spread_price` (negative when crossed), `spread_bps` (rounded half-up to 2 decimals), `crossed`, `funded_total` per side and `depth_bands` (funded base quantity per side within 10, 50 and 100 bps of `mid`, bounds included). `best_bid` or `best_ask` is `null` when its side is empty or its best price is zero, and `mid`, `spread_price`, `spread_bps`, `crossed` and `depth_bands` are then `null` too. The optional `domain` (a PermissionedDomain id) reads that domain's permissioned order book instead of the open book. `base` equal to `quote` (same currency and issuer) is a 400 naming `quote`.

When to use: To read executable liquidity for a pair on the XRPL central limit order book (CLOB).

When not to use: Not for AMM liquidity (use the amm page) and not for a cost estimate (use the slippage page).

get.summary: Slippage and average price for buying or selling an amount of base currency.
get.description:
Walks the asks (side=buy, the default) or the bids (side=sell) of the cached order book to estimate the average price and `slippage_pct` (a percentage; on a partial fill, of the filled part; `null` when nothing is filled or there is no best price) of buying or selling `amount` of `base` for `quote`. As on `/v1/xrpl/orderbook`, offers whose expiry is at or before the close time of the latest validated ledger are left out of the walk, possibly slightly early, `meta` also covers that latest-ledger read, and when its close time cannot be read the answer fails as a failed read does (503 `upstream-unavailable`). `depth` echoes the requested depth (100 when absent) and `depth_effective` reports the bucket served (10, 50 or 100). The transfer fee is that of the asset the taker sends (quote on a buy, base on a sell), reported when it can be loaded as `transfer_fee_pct`, in percent ((TransferRate - 1000000000) / 10000000, exact; `null` when the rate cannot be loaded); XRP has none (`"0"`). Slippage models an OfferCreate taker: a cross-currency Payment also charges the received asset's TransferRate, which `/v1/xrpl/paths` accounts for. The top-level fields describe the CLOB fill: `insufficient_liquidity` is true when `amount` cannot be fully filled or there is no best price, `partial` is true when `filled` is above 0 and below `amount`, and a partial fill reports `avg_price`, `slippage_pct` and `avg_price_after_fees` of the filled part. `worst_price` is the price of the worst book level the reported fill reaches (the last level consumed), quote per base, `null` when nothing is filled. `venues` compares the CLOB with the AMM pool for the same amount (`best` is the venue with the better average price for the side: lower on a buy, higher on a sell; ties go to the CLOB; no routing split) and `venues.amm_status` is `ok`, `stale`, `no_pool`, `frozen` (a pool asset is frozen, so the pool is not used) or `unavailable`. The venues compare full fills only: on a partial fill `venues.clob` carries `null` prices and is never `best`. `venues.amm` is `null` when the pair has no pool, the pool is empty or frozen, or it could not be read (see amm_status); the response never fails because of the AMM. With `domain`, the AMM is not read: `venues.amm` is `null`, `venues.amm_status` is `no_pool` and the venue ages are `null`. CLOB slippage is measured against the best ask (side=buy) or the best bid (side=sell) and AMM slippage against the pool spot price (so it includes the trading fee). `base` equal to `quote` (same currency and issuer) is a 400 naming `quote`.

When to use: Before placing a market-style trade, to size it against available depth and to see whether the CLOB or the AMM pool gives the better average price for the side.

When not to use: It is an estimate, not a quote, and it does not split an amount across venues or route through other pairs. To read pool reserves, use the amm page.

get.summary: AMM pool reserves and trading fee for an asset pair.
get.description:
Returns the reserves of both assets in the order requested, matched to `a` and `b` by currency and issuer (XRP by type), each asset echoed as `asset_a` and `asset_b` with `asset_a_currency_ascii` and `asset_b_currency_ascii` right after them for a 40-hex currency code (its readable text, `null` when not printable ASCII; absent for XRP and 3-character codes), and the trading fee in percent, `trading_fee_pct` (TradingFee / 1000, exact: `0.5` is 0.5 %). `spot_a_per_b` (reserve_a / reserve_b) and `spot_b_per_a` (reserve_b / reserve_a) are the fee-free pool prices; their `_with_fee` variants divide them by (1 - trading_fee_pct / 100), the marginal price a taker pays. `lp_token` gives the LP token's currency, its `currency_ascii` (`null`: an AMM LP code starts with 0x03, not printable), issuer (the AMM account) and outstanding supply, and `a_per_lp_token` and `b_per_lp_token` each reserve divided by that supply. `auction_slot` is active while unexpired at the read ledger, with its discounted fee in percent (`discounted_fee_pct`) and its expiry time; it is `null` when no account holds the slot. It names, from the `amm_info` auction slot, the holder, `auction_slot.account` (the slot's `Account`), the up to 4 further accounts at the discounted fee, `auth_accounts` (`AuthAccounts`, empty when none), the `price` the holder paid in LP tokens (`Price`, exact), its expiry `expires_at` (`Expiration`), the current 1/20 interval of the 24-hour slot, `time_interval` (which rippled computes from the parent ledger close time; 20 once expired, `null` when the node omits it), and `outbid_price`, the LP tokens to outbid the holder now by rippled `AMMBid.cpp` at that interval (price × 1.05 + `auction_slot_minimum_price` in interval 0, price × 1.05 × (1 − ((interval + 1) / 20)^60) + `auction_slot_minimum_price` after it, `auction_slot_minimum_price` once expired; rounded half-up to at most 18 places, while rippled computes it in `Number` with a 16-digit mantissa, so the last digits can differ; `null` when the interval is unknown). The top-level `auction_slot_minimum_price`, served also when no account holds the slot, is the LP tokens to take a vacant or expired slot (LPTokenBalance × TradingFee / 100000 / 25, rounded half-up to at most 18 places), and `vote_slots` lists the trading-fee votes in the order `amm_info` lists them, each with its `account` (the vote slot's `Account`, an LP holder), its voted fee in percent (`trading_fee_pct`, TradingFee / 1000, exact) and its weight as a ratio (`vote_weight_ratio`, VoteWeight / 100000, exact), empty without votes. `a_frozen` and `b_frozen` report whether each asset is frozen, so the pool cannot be traded. `vote_dispersion` gives the number of trading-fee votes, the lowest and highest voted fee in percent (`min_fee_pct`, `max_fee_pct`) and the vote-weighted standard deviation of the voted fees in percent (`weighted_sd_pct`, rounded once to 18 places; `null` when the weights sum to zero); it is `null` without votes. For an empty pool (a zero reserve or LP supply) the four spot prices, `a_per_lp_token` and `b_per_lp_token` are `null`. `a` equal to `b` (same currency and issuer) is a 400 naming `b`.

When to use: To read AMM pool depth and fee for a pair.

When not to use: It does not estimate slippage or compare venues (use the slippage page for the CLOB vs AMM comparison); a pair without a pool returns 404.

get.summary: XRP balance, sequence, owner count, transfer rate and trust lines (capped) for an account.
get.description:
Returns the XRP balance as a decimal string, `sequence`, `owner_count`, the account transfer fee in percent, `transfer_fee_pct` ((TransferRate - 1000000000) / 10000000, exact; `"0"` when the account sets none), the account `flags` decoded to booleans (`require_dest_tag`, `deposit_auth`, `disallow_xrp`, `disallow_incoming` for checks, NFToken offers, payment channels and trust lines, `require_auth`, `default_ripple`, `global_freeze`, `no_freeze`, `allow_clawback`, `disable_master`, `allow_trustline_locking`) and up to 50 trust lines. It also reports `ticket_count` (`TicketCount`, 0 when absent), `sponsored_owner_count`, `sponsoring_owner_count` and `sponsoring_account_count` (`SponsoredOwnerCount`, `SponsoringOwnerCount`, `SponsoringAccountCount`; null when absent: the Sponsor amendment is not enabled), the key control and identity fields `regular_key` (`RegularKey`), `signer_list_set` (true when the account has a `SignerList`), `domain` (`Domain`, decoded to text) and `tick_size` (`TickSize`) (each null when absent), and `amm_id`, `vault_id` and `loan_broker_id` (`AMMID`, `VaultID`, `LoanBrokerID`), set only when the account is that pseudo-account, else null. `flags.disable_master` is `lsfDisableMaster` and `flags.allow_trustline_locking` is `lsfAllowTrustLineLocking`. Each trust line carries `peer` (the counterparty), `currency` (with `currency_ascii` for a 40-hex code), `role` (`issuer` when the balance is negative, else `holder`), `balance` and `line_limit` (the limit the account sets). `lines_truncated` is `true` whenever upstream has more lines. `is_issuer` is `true` when any fetched line balance is negative, `null` when none is and `lines_truncated` is `true`, else `false`.

When to use: To inspect an account before building a transaction for it.

When not to use: Not for transaction history or reserves; it is a summary, not a full account dump.

get.summary: One page of an account's trust lines, with an opaque cursor for the next page.
get.description:
Returns one page of trust lines: peer, canonical currency, balance, `line_limit` (the limit the account sets), `peer_line_limit` (the limit the peer sets) and the `no_ripple`, `freeze` and `authorized` flags of both sides; amounts are decimal strings. Each line also carries `role` (`issuer` when the balance is negative, else `holder`), `headroom` (holder only: `line_limit` minus balance; `null` for an issuer), `deep_freeze` and `deep_freeze_peer` (always booleans, `false` when not set) and `quality_in_multiplier` and `quality_out_multiplier`, the line's QualityIn and QualityOut as factors (value / 1e9, 1 = unchanged; absent or 0 means 1). `limit` is the page size, 10 to 400 lines (default 100), `peer` keeps only lines with that counterparty, and `marker` is an opaque cursor: send it back unchanged to get the next page; it is `null` on the last page and only valid for the address that produced it.

When to use: To list every trust line of an account (balances, limits, freeze and authorization flags), page by page.

When not to use: For a quick capped overview with the XRP balance, use `/v1/xrpl/account/{address}/summary`; for issued totals of a token, use the token endpoint.

get.summary: One page of an account's most recent validated transactions, newest first.
get.description:
Returns one page of the account's most recent validated transactions, newest first, in a compact shape: hash, ledger index, close time, transaction type, result code, counterparty (when the transaction names one) and delivered amount as a decimal string (when reported; `delivered` is `null` and `delivered_unavailable` is `true` when the ledger reports it as unavailable, and an MPT amount is `{asset: <MPT issuance id>, value: null, value_atomic}`: its exact base units in `value_atomic`, and `value` null because this route reads no issuance). Each entry also carries `direction` (`out`, `in` or `other`), `fee_xrp` (`out` only), `partial_payment`, `destination_tag`, `source_tag` (the sender's `SourceTag`), `invoice_id` (the `InvoiceID`, 64-hex as the ledger holds it; each tag and `invoice_id` `null` when absent) and `balance_changes` (the address's signed net changes as `{asset, value}`; a 40-hex currency code also carries `currency_ascii`). `limit` is 1 to 50 transactions (default 20) and is honored per response: a response returns at most `limit` entries. `marker` is an opaque cursor: send it back unchanged, even with a different `limit`, to get the next (older) entries; it resumes after the last returned entry, so no entry is skipped or repeated. A response never spans two upstream pages, so it can hold fewer than `limit` entries before the last page. `marker` is `null` on the last page and only valid for the address that produced it. No history depth is promised: history depth depends on the serving node (how far back pages go depends on the ledger history of the node that serves the request), and older pages may be slower because they can be served by a node that keeps a longer history.

When to use: To check what an account did recently (payments sent or received, offers, trust line changes) and whether each transaction succeeded.

When not to use: For balances and trust lines, use `/v1/xrpl/account/{address}/summary` or `/v1/xrpl/account/{address}/lines`; for full archival history, use a full-history node or indexer: history depth depends on the serving node and older pages may be slower.

get.summary: Issuer data for an issued asset: flags, domain, transfer fee and total issued.
get.description:
Returns the issuer data for an issued asset `CODE.issuer`: the issuer flags under `flags`, decoded as the account summary decodes its `flags` (`require_dest_tag`, `deposit_auth`, `disallow_xrp`, `disallow_incoming` for checks, NFToken offers, payment channels and trust lines, `require_auth`, `default_ripple`, `global_freeze`, `no_freeze`, `allow_clawback`, `disable_master`, `allow_trustline_locking`), `tick_size` (null when unset) and `blackholed`, the issuer `domain` decoded to text when set, `transfer_fee_pct` (the issuer transfer fee in percent: (TransferRate - 1000000000) / 10000000, exact; `"0"` without a fee), and `obligations`, the total issued of that currency as a decimal string (`"0"` when the issuer has not issued it). `amm_id`, `vault_id` and `loan_broker_id` (`AMMID`, `VaultID`, `LoanBrokerID`) are set only when the issuer is that pseudo-account, else null; `frozen_obligations` sums this currency's `frozen_balances` of `gateway_balances` (frozen lines, outside `obligations`) and `locked_obligations` is its `locked` amount (held in escrow), each `"0"` when there is none. When the node cannot report obligations, the response is still 200 with `obligations`, `frozen_obligations` and `locked_obligations` null and `obligations_status: "unavailable"`. The body opens with `asset`, the queried token in the canonical form the route reads (its readable text is `currency_ascii`). Holder counts are not returned.

When to use: Before accepting or sending an issued token: check that the issuer exists, is not frozen, whether holders need authorization, and the transfer fee charged on every transfer between non-issuer accounts.

When not to use: For XRP (not an issued asset; 400), for one account's own balances use `/v1/xrpl/account/{address}/lines`, and for prices use `/v1/xrpl/orderbook` or `/v1/xrpl/amm/{a}/{b}`.

get.summary: Pre-payment check: can this payment from source to destination succeed now?
get.description:
Checks, before you sign, whether a payment of `asset` (default `XRP`) from `source` to `destination` can succeed on the validated ledger, and returns a `verdict`: `ready`, `not_ready` (at least one blocking reason) or `unknown` (no blocking reason, but a sub-check could not run; never treat `unknown` as `ready`). `asset` may also be a 48-hex MPT issuance id, whose `amount` is a whole number of base units. For an MPT, `amount` is echoed in those base units, and `required_source_balance` and `max_sendable` carry `value_atomic` (whole base units) and `value` in display units (`value_atomic` / 10^`AssetScale`), null when the issuance could not be read. A missing account is a reason, not an error: this endpoint never answers 404. Without `amount` the amount-dependent checks are skipped. `spendable_xrp` is the source XRP above the larger of its live reserve (base plus owner count times increment, from the server state) and the `standard` fee tier; the body states those inputs as `reserve_base_xrp` and `reserve_inc_xrp` (in XRP), `source_owner_count` and `fee_drops` (the `standard` tier, in drops), each `null` when its read failed or the source is missing, and `source_balance` is the source's balance of `asset` (an MPT in both units; zero when it holds no trust line or MPToken; `null` when that read failed, the source is missing or it is the asset's issuer); `transfer_fee_pct` is the issuer transfer fee when it applies. `required_source_balance` is what the source must hold for `amount` (XRP: the amount plus the larger of the reserve and the fee; a token sent between two holders: the amount plus the transfer fee; `null` without `amount` or when a figure is unknown), and `max_sendable` is the most the source's balance allows it to send now, rounded down (freezes, limits and authorization are reported as reasons, not deducted; `null` when the source is the issuer of a trust-line token or a figure is unknown; for the issuer of an MPT, the room left below the issuance's maximum amount). For an MPT sent between two holders, the fee-inclusive cost is rounded to whole base units by the rule the network has enabled: up once the `fixCleanup3_5_0` amendment is enabled or when its state is unknown; before it, to nearest with ties to even when the exact cost has at most 16 significant digits, else up. `required_source_balance` is that rounded cost, `insufficient_token_balance` compares the balance with it, and `max_sendable` is the largest whole amount whose rounded cost fits the balance (without `amount` the amendment state is not read and the cost rounds up). Warnings never change the verdict. The `deposit_authorized` sub-check also covers `credentials`. An MPT payment between two holders with `amount` also reads the network's amendment state, which is network configuration, changed only at flag ledgers after an amendment vote, and is not counted in the answer's `meta`. `meta.ledger_index` is `null`, never 0, when no read behind the answer names a ledger.

Reason codes: `source_not_found`, `insufficient_xrp_balance`, `source_line_missing`, `insufficient_token_balance`, `source_line_frozen`, `destination_not_found`, `amount_below_destination_reserve`, `destination_tag_required`, `deposit_not_authorized`, `credentials_invalid`, `destination_line_missing`, `destination_line_limit_exceeded`, `destination_line_frozen`, `destination_line_unauthorized`, `issuer_not_found`, `issuer_global_freeze`, `issuer_rippling_disabled`, `destination_is_pseudo_account`, `mpt_issuance_not_found`, `source_mpt_missing`, `destination_mpt_missing`, `source_mpt_unauthorized`, `destination_mpt_unauthorized`, `mpt_locked`, `mpt_transfer_disabled`, `mpt_max_amount_exceeded`.

Warning codes: `destination_will_be_created`, `transfer_fee`, `high_fee`, `network_degraded`, `credentials_unchecked`.

Sub-check codes: `source_account`, `destination_account`, `deposit_authorized`, `source_line`, `destination_line`, `issuer`, `mpt_issuance`, `source_mpt`, `destination_mpt`, `fee`, `network_health`.

| Reason code | Blocks when |
|---|---|
| `source_not_found` | the source account does not exist |
| `insufficient_xrp_balance` | an XRP `amount` exceeds `spendable_xrp` |
| `source_line_missing` | the source, not the issuer, has no trust line to the issuer |
| `insufficient_token_balance` | the source's trust line or MPToken balance is below `amount`, plus the transfer fee between two holders |
| `source_line_frozen` | the issuer froze or deep froze the source line, unless the destination is the issuer |
| `destination_not_found` | a token payment's destination does not exist |
| `amount_below_destination_reserve` | an XRP payment to a missing destination is below the base reserve |
| `destination_tag_required` | the destination requires a tag and `destination_tag` is not given |
| `deposit_not_authorized` | the destination requires deposit authorization and has not authorized the source (an XRP `amount` at most the base reserve to a destination holding at most the base reserve is exempt) |
| `credentials_invalid` | `deposit_authorized` rejects the given `credentials` |
| `destination_line_missing` | the destination, not the issuer, has no trust line to the issuer |
| `destination_line_limit_exceeded` | the destination line's limit minus its balance is below `amount` |
| `destination_line_frozen` | the issuer deep froze the destination line, unless the source is the issuer (a regular freeze does not block receiving) |
| `destination_line_unauthorized` | the issuer requires authorization and has not authorized the destination line |
| `issuer_not_found` | the issuer account does not exist |
| `issuer_global_freeze` | the issuer froze all its tokens, for a payment between two holders |
| `issuer_rippling_disabled` | between two holders, the issuer set NoRipple on both lines |
| `destination_is_pseudo_account` | the destination is an AMM, Vault or LoanBroker pseudo-account |
| `mpt_issuance_not_found` | the MPT issuance does not exist |
| `source_mpt_missing` | the source, not the issuer, holds no MPToken of the issuance |
| `destination_mpt_missing` | the destination, not the issuer, holds no MPToken of the issuance |
| `source_mpt_unauthorized` | the issuance requires authorization and the source's MPToken is not authorized |
| `destination_mpt_unauthorized` | the issuance requires authorization and the destination's MPToken is not authorized |
| `mpt_locked` | between two holders, the issuance or either holder's MPToken is locked |
| `mpt_transfer_disabled` | between two holders, the issuance does not allow transfers |
| `mpt_max_amount_exceeded` | the issuer would send more than the issuance's maximum amount allows |

| Warning code | Reported when |
|---|---|
| `destination_will_be_created` | an XRP payment creates the destination account |
| `transfer_fee` | the issuer charges a transfer fee between two holders (`transfer_fee_pct`); set `SendMax` to at least `required_source_balance`, or the payment fails with `tecPATH_PARTIAL` |
| `high_fee` | the fee band is high |
| `network_degraded` | network health is degraded or down |
| `credentials_unchecked` | the destination does not exist, so `credentials` could not be checked |

When to use: Right before sending a payment: to catch a missing or unfunded destination, a required destination tag, deposit authorization, missing or frozen trust lines, MPT authorization and locks, insufficient balance and issuer freezes, in one call.

When not to use: To find a multi-hop route or the source amount needed for a cross-currency payment (use the paths endpoint), or to list balances (use `/v1/xrpl/account/{address}/summary`).

get.summary: Multi-hop payment paths and their source cost.
get.description:
Runs a live path search (`ripple_path_find`) on the validated ledger for delivering `amount` of `asset` from `source` to `destination`, and returns the `alternatives`: each with the estimated `source_amount` the source would spend (`{asset, value}`, an MPT one as `{asset, value: null, value_atomic}`: its exact base units in `value_atomic`, and `value` null because this route reads no issuance), `paths_count`, the computed `paths` as compact steps (`account`, `currency`, `issuer`), `effective_price` (`source_amount` / `amount`, an MPT source in its base units), `cheapest` (the lowest `source_amount` among the alternatives with the same source asset) and `suggested_send_max` (`source_amount` × 1.01, rounded up to the asset precision: whole drops for XRP, whole base units for an MPT and 15 significant digits for issued currencies). Each alternative also carries `source_any_issuer`, true when rippled names the source account as the issuer of `source_amount`, meaning the source may spend that currency from any issuer it holds (false for XRP). The body echoes `source`, `destination`, `asset`, `amount`, `send_max_asset`, `send_max` and `source_assets` after `alternatives`, assets in the canonical form the route reads, `amount` and `send_max` as the request sent them and `source_assets` in request order; `send_max_asset`, `send_max` and `source_assets` are `null` when the request sent none. A call can take up to about 20 seconds, because path finding is heavy for the node. Results are best effort: `paths_may_be_non_optimal` is always `true`, a cheaper path may exist and the amounts are estimates that can change by the time you submit. No alternative is a 200 with `alternatives: []`. A destination account that does not exist gives `alternatives: []` and the warning `destination_not_found`; a source account that does not exist is a 404. When the node's answer names no ledger (as on a destination that does not exist, which the node reports as an error), `meta.ledger_index` is `null`, never 0. Answers are never cached: every call reads the ledger.

When to use: Before a cross-currency or multi-hop payment: to see whether a route exists and how much the source would spend to deliver the amount. A call can take up to about 20 seconds and paths may be non-optimal.

When not to use: To check whether a direct payment can succeed (use `/v1/xrpl/payment-readiness`), or for the single-hop cost of a trade on one pair (use `/v1/xrpl/slippage`, which compares the order book and the AMM).

get.summary: MPT issuance: issuer, supply, scale, transfer fee and flags.
get.description:
Reads one Multi-Purpose Token (MPT) issuance from the validated ledger with one `ledger_entry` call, and echoes `mpt_issuance_id` in the upper-case hex the route reads. Amounts are display values, the base units divided by 10^`asset_scale`, each with an `_atomic` twin holding the integer string of base units: `maximum_amount` (`null` when the issuance sets none; the ledger then allows up to 9223372036854775807 base units), `outstanding_amount`, `confidential_outstanding_amount` (`ConfidentialOutstandingAmount`, the part of `outstanding_amount` held in confidential balances, already included in it; `0` when none), and `locked_amount` (`null` when none is locked in escrow). `transfer_fee_pct` is the fee the issuer charges on transfers between holders, in percent. `flags` decodes the issuance flags, `can_hold_confidential_balance` included; `immutable_flags` decodes `ImmutableFlags`, one boolean per setting that can never change: a flag of the same name, or, for `metadata` and `transfer_fee`, the issuance's `MPTokenMetadata` and `TransferFee` (all `false` when the issuance has none). `transferable` is true when `can_transfer` is set and the issuance is not locked; `utilization_ratio` is `outstanding_amount_atomic / maximum_amount_atomic`, and `headroom`, with its `_atomic` twin, is `maximum_amount - outstanding_amount`, exact: what the issuer can still issue; without a maximum, both are computed against the protocol cap 9223372036854775807 base units. `metadata_present` says whether the issuer set metadata, and `issuer_encryption_key_present` and `auditor_encryption_key_present` whether it set `IssuerEncryptionKey` and `AuditorEncryptionKey`; the metadata and the key values are not served. `domain_id` is the issuance's `DomainID` (`null` when none). A missing issuance answers 404 `not-found`.

When to use: Before accepting or sending an MPT: to check its issuer, decimal scale, supply against its maximum, transfer fee, and whether it can be transferred, locked, escrowed or clawed back.

When not to use: To check whether one MPT payment between two accounts can succeed now (use `/v1/xrpl/payment-readiness` with the issuance id as `asset`), or for a trust-line token written `CODE.issuer` (use `/v1/xrpl/token/{asset}`).

get.summary: What kind of XRPL address is this, and what does a payment to it need?
get.description:
Reads the account at `address` on the latest validated ledger with one `account_info` call. The body echoes the queried `address`. `kind` is `not_found` (no account; still a 200 answer), `amm`, `vault` or `loan_broker` (the pseudo-account of an AMM pool, a vault or a loan broker, read from `AMMID`, `VaultID` or `LoanBrokerID`), or `account`. `amm_id`, `vault_id` and `loan_broker_id` carry that field of a pseudo-account, else null. `flags` are the decoded AccountRoot flags, `regular_key` (`RegularKey`, null when absent) and `signer_list_set` are the key-control inputs of `blackholed`, and `blackholed` is true when the master key is disabled, there is no signer list and the regular key is absent or a known blackhole address; for `not_found`, the ids, `flags`, `regular_key`, `signer_list_set` and `blackholed` are null. Payment hints: destination_tag_required, deposit_preauth_required, xrp_not_wanted (advisory: the ledger does not enforce it), pseudo_account_rejects_payments, blackholed_account.

When to use: Before paying or listing an XRPL address: to learn whether it exists, whether it is a pseudo-account that rejects payments, and whether a payment needs a destination tag or deposit preauthorization.

When not to use: To check one payment end to end with amounts, trust lines and reserves (use `/v1/xrpl/payment-readiness`), or to read balances (use `/v1/xrpl/account/{address}/summary`).

get.summary: Is this XRPL issued currency the canonical stablecoin it claims to be?
get.description:
Answers from a closed registry of canonical stablecoins, each entry taken from the issuer's own documentation. `canonical` is true only for a registry asset, and `registry_entry` then names the issuer and links its own documentation. `posture` is the issuer's controls read live on the latest validated ledger (`global_freeze`, `allow_clawback`, `require_auth`, `no_freeze` and `transfer_fee_pct`) and compared with a dated snapshot: `posture_matches_registry` says whether every fact still matches, and `posture_differences` lists each one that changed as `<field>_changed`. `issuer_key_control` (`disable_master`, `regular_key`, `signer_list_set`) says who can sign for the issuer now, from the same read as `posture` and never compared with the snapshot; it is null for a non-registry asset or when the issuer is not found. A registry issuer whose account is missing answers `posture: null` with `issuer_not_found`, still 200. `impersonation_risk` is computed from the request alone, with no upstream call: it is true when the currency code is a registry code but the issuer is not its canonical issuer, and `canonical_issuer` then names that issuer. The body opens with `asset`, the queried asset as canonical `CODE.issuer`, with its readable text in `asset_currency_ascii` for a 40-hex code. No regulatory or licensing status is returned, and a canonical answer is not an endorsement of the token.

When to use: Before accepting or quoting a stablecoin: to check the asset is the canonical one and that its issuer facts have not changed since the snapshot.

When not to use: To read supply or balances (use `/v1/xrpl/token/{asset}` or `/v1/xrpl/account/{address}/lines`), or as a regulatory or licensing check: none is served.

A standard code uses letters, digits or `?!@#$%^&*<>(){}[]|` and is never `XRP`; percent-encode the symbols in a URL (for example `%3F` for `?`). A 40-hex code is read in any case, and the 40-hex form of a standard code means that code.

get.summary: Did this settled payment deliver the expected asset and amount to the expected account?
get.description:
Reads the transaction `hash` once and compares what it delivered with what you expected, returning a derived `verdict` and nothing else about the account. The answer is never an error when the transaction is absent: `not_found` (definitive, the transaction was never validated and no longer can be), `not_found_recent` (not found in the server's history window, not definitive), `beyond_history` (the searched range falls outside the server's history, not definitive) and `not_final` (it can still be validated) are verdicts with a 200. The other verdicts are `not_a_payment`, `failed` (the result was not `tesSUCCESS`), `wrong_recipient`, `wrong_sender` (only with `source`), `wrong_destination_tag` (only with `destination_tag`), `unverifiable` (the ledger does not state what was delivered), `wrong_asset`, `underpaid` (less than `amount` was delivered) and `paid`. The first verdict that matches, in that order, is the one returned.

| Verdict | What settles it | Definitive |
|---|---|---|
| `not_found` | `txnNotFound` with `last_ledger_sequence` given, at or below the latest validated ledger, and the whole range searched: the transaction was never validated and can no longer be | definitive |
| `not_found_recent` | `txnNotFound` without `last_ledger_sequence`: not found in the server's history window | not definitive |
| `beyond_history` | `txnNotFound` with `last_ledger_sequence` at or below the latest validated ledger, but the answer does not confirm the whole range was searched | not definitive |
| `not_final` | the transaction is not validated yet, or `last_ledger_sequence` is above the latest validated ledger: it can still be validated | not definitive |
| `not_a_payment` | the transaction is not a `Payment` | definitive |
| `failed` | the result is not `tesSUCCESS` | definitive |
| `wrong_recipient` | `Destination` differs from `destination` | definitive |
| `wrong_sender` | `source` is given and `Account` differs | definitive |
| `wrong_destination_tag` | `destination_tag` is given and the transaction carries none or another | definitive |
| `unverifiable` | the ledger does not state what was delivered | definitive |
| `wrong_asset` | the delivered asset differs from `asset` | definitive |
| `underpaid` | less than `amount` was delivered | definitive |
| `paid` | none of the above applies | definitive |

`failure_code` is the `TransactionResult` of a validated transaction that did not succeed (not `tesSUCCESS`), such as `tecPATH_DRY`, whatever the verdict, so a failed transaction that is not a `Payment` carries it too; a result that does not match `^[A-Za-z0-9_]{1,40}$` is reported as `unknown_error`. It is `null` when there is no transaction, when the transaction is not validated yet (`not_final`) and when it succeeded. `delivered` is always the amount the ledger says was delivered, never the amount the payer asked to send, so a partial payment is reported as it settled and `partial_payment` says whether the payment allowed one. `excess` is what was delivered above `amount` on a `paid` verdict, the same `{asset, value}` amount object as `expected` and `delivered`, and `null` otherwise. An MPT `expected`, `delivered` or `excess` also carries `value_atomic`, its exact base units, and a `value` of `null`, since the verify reads no MPT issuance and so no `AssetScale`. `settled_at` is the close time of the ledger holding the transaction (`ledger_index`), `null` when the node's answer carries no readable close time; with no transaction to read, `delivered`, `excess`, `ledger_index` and `settled_at` are `null`. `valuation` is an informative EUR and USD reference value given only on a `paid` or `underpaid` verdict for a registry stablecoin when an ECB rate on or before the payment date is stored; otherwise it is `null`. The value is an informative reference, not a tax figure. Source: ECB statistics. The transaction's own `DestinationTag` is `transaction_destination_tag` and its `InvoiceID` is `invoice_id` (64-hex as the ledger holds it), each `null` when absent or when there is no transaction. After `valuation` the body echoes the queried `hash`, `destination`, `destination_tag`, `source` and `last_ledger_sequence` (each optional one `null` when the request sent none). Pass the `LastLedgerSequence` you signed as `last_ledger_sequence`: without it an absent transaction can only answer `not_found_recent`, which is not definitive. A validated transaction never changes and a definitive `not_found` cannot change, so those answers are fresh for 86400 seconds and served stale for up to 604800; `not_found_recent`, `beyond_history` and `not_final` are fresh for 4 seconds and served stale for up to 30. If the upstream read fails, an answer cached within its stale window is served instead of a 503. When the node's answer for a found transaction names no ledger, `ledger_index` and `meta.ledger_index` are `null`, never 0.

When to use: After a payment has been submitted: to confirm from the ledger that it delivered the asset and amount you expected to the account you expected, including the partial-payment case.

When not to use: Before sending a payment (use `/v1/xrpl/payment-readiness`), or to list an account's recent payments (use `/v1/xrpl/account/{address}/transactions`).

get.summary: Can this payer settle this x402 payment requirement right now?
get.description:
Takes one x402 v2 `exact` requirement as an XRPL server states it (`asset` with its `issuer` from `extra.issuer`, `amount`, `pay_to`, and `destination_tag` from `extra.destinationTag`) plus the `payer` wallet, and answers one `verdict`: `block` on any blocker, `warn` with warnings only, else `ok`. `amount` is in drops for XRP and in token units for an issued currency; drops are converted to XRP and `destination_tag` is passed on before the payer's payment readiness is evaluated for that payment. `readiness` is what `/v1/xrpl/payment-readiness` answers for the same payer, recipient, asset and amount, without its `meta`, so both routes can be compared field by field; each readiness blocking reason becomes the blocker `payer_<code>` and each readiness warning the warning `payer_<code>`. A `pay_to` that is an AMM, vault or loan broker pseudo-account is the blocker `pay_to_not_wallet`, and `destination_is_pseudo_account` is then not repeated as `payer_destination_is_pseudo_account`; every other readiness code is still copied. A readiness `verdict` of `unknown` gives the warning `payer_readiness_unknown`, so never read a `warn` as a cleared payment. An issued `asset` that is not a canonical stablecoin of the registry gives the warning `asset_not_canonical`; `XRP` is not compared with the registry and never gives it. `pay_to` must differ from `payer`: the same address is a 400 naming `pay_to`, and nothing is read. The check makes exactly the readiness reads and no others. `meta.ledger_index` is `null`, never 0, when no read behind the answer names a ledger.

| Code | What it states | Blocks or warns |
|---|---|---|
| `pay_to_not_wallet` | `pay_to` is an AMM, vault or loan broker pseudo-account | blocks |
| `asset_not_canonical` | `asset` is not the canonical stablecoin of the registry (never `XRP`) | warns |
| `payer_readiness_unknown` | the payer's readiness `verdict` is `unknown`, so the payment is not cleared | warns |
| `payer_*` | every applicable payer readiness blocker or reason appears with the prefix `payer_` (`payer_<code>`), and each readiness warning appears as the warning `payer_<code>`; the codes are those of `/v1/xrpl/payment-readiness` | blocks or warns, as the readiness code does |

When to use: After an x402 server answered 402 with an XRPL `exact` requirement: to check, before signing, that this payer can settle that exact requirement to that recipient now.

When not to use: For a payment that is not an x402 requirement (use `/v1/xrpl/payment-readiness`), or once the payment has settled (use `/v1/xrpl/payment/verify`).

get.summary: Is this account a member of this XRPL permissioned domain, as its owner or through an accepted, unexpired credential?
get.description:
Reads the PermissionedDomain `domain_id` from the validated ledger with one `ledger_entry` call, then each credential the domain accepts with `account` as its subject, the owner included (one `ledger_entry` call each, in parallel), together with the latest validated ledger, whose close time decides expiry. The answer echoes `domain_id`, in the upper-case hex the route reads, and `account`. Each row of `credentials` has a `status`: `missing` (the account holds no such credential), `expired` (its `Expiration` is before the validated ledger close time; one equal to the close time is still valid), `not_accepted` (the account has not accepted it), `valid`, or `unknown` (its read failed, or it has an `Expiration` and the close time could not be read). An expired credential is `expired` even when it is not accepted. Each verdict answers its own uses and is `eligible`, `not_eligible` or `unknown`. `credential_verdict` judges the account's credentials against the domain, for MPT `DomainID` authorization and private vault deposits, with no owner exemption: `eligible` when any credential is `valid`, `unknown` when none is valid and any is `unknown`, else `not_eligible`. Two protocol uses add their own rules: the owner of a private vault deposits into it without a domain check, and an account that already holds an MPToken passes MPT authorization even when `validDomain` fails. `dex_verdict` is membership for trading in the domain's permissioned order books: the owner is `eligible` with `dex_membership: "owner"` whatever its credentials; any other account takes its `credential_verdict`, with `dex_membership: "credential"` when `eligible`, else `null`. Each `unknown` credential is named in `checks_failed` as `credential:<issuer>:<credential_type>`. `matched_credential` is the first `valid` credential in the domain's order, the owner's included; `null` when none is valid. The rows of `credentials` and `matched_credential` also carry the credential's `expires_at` (its `Expiration`, ISO 8601 UTC, `null` without one) and `uri` (its `URI`, hex as the ledger stores it, `null` when absent), both `null` when the credential is missing or its read failed. Each found credential carries its `credential_id`, its ledger entry index, which `/v1/xrpl/payment-readiness` takes in `credentials`. `credential_type` is in ledger hex; `credential_type_ascii` is its text when every byte is printable ASCII, else `null`. A missing domain answers 404 `not-found`. Every answer, the owner's included, is fresh for 4 seconds, the policy of its latest-ledger read.

When to use: Before trading in a permissioned order book (`/v1/xrpl/orderbook` or `/v1/xrpl/slippage` with `domain`): to check whether an account is a member of the domain, as its owner or through an accepted, unexpired credential, and which credential qualifies it.

When not to use: To check whether one payment can succeed now (use `/v1/xrpl/payment-readiness`, whose `credentials` takes the `credential_id` values of this answer), or to read the permissioned order book itself (use `/v1/xrpl/orderbook` with `domain`).

get.summary: One page of an account's open DEX offers, with how funded each one is.
get.description:
Returns one page of the account's open DEX offers from the validated ledger, in the ledger's order. Each offer has `seq` (the sequence number of the transaction that created it), `sells` (TakerGets) and `buys` (TakerPays) as `{asset, value}` (XRP in XRP, not drops; a 40-hex currency code also carries `currency_ascii`; an MPT one is `{asset, value: null, value_atomic}`, its exact base units in `value_atomic` and `value` null because this route reads no issuance), `price` (buys / sells, an MPT side in its base units, `null` when `sells` is zero), `funded_ratio`, `expires_at` (ISO 8601 UTC, `null` without an `Expiration`), `expired` (`true` when the `Expiration` is at or before the validated ledger close time) and the offer flags `passive`, `sell` and `hybrid` (`lsfHybrid`: the offer sits in a permissioned domain's book and in the open book). `funded_ratio` is min(1, available / `sells`), computed for each offer on its own, so offers that share a balance are not netted: available is the spendable XRP (the balance minus the reserve, never below 0) for an offer selling XRP, and for a token the trust line balance (a negative one counts as 0) divided by the issuer's TransferRate / 1e9. It is `1` when the account issues the token it sells, and `0` when the issuer froze the line or all its tokens, when the lines page is complete and holds no line for the token, or when the line of the token the offer buys is deep-frozen by its issuer. It is `null` for an MPT, when the line of the token it sells or buys may lie beyond the 400-line page the route reads, for the offers selling tokens of issuers beyond the first 10 distinct issuers of the page, and when a read it needs failed. Each failed read is named in `checks_failed` (`account`, `lines`, `issuer:<address>`, `ledger`, `reserves`); a failed `ledger` read leaves `expired` `null` for the offers with an `Expiration`. `totals` counts the offers of this page (`offer_count`) and the `unfunded` ones (`funded_ratio` `0`). Besides the page, the route reads only what its offers need: the account entry and the reserves when an offer sells XRP, one page of up to 400 trust lines when an offer sells or buys a token the account does not issue, the account entry of the issuer of each such token an offer sells, and the latest validated ledger when an offer has an `Expiration`. `limit` is 10 to 50 offers (default 20), and `marker` is an opaque cursor: send it back unchanged to get the next page; it is `null` on the last page and only valid for the address that produced it. A page can hold fewer than `limit` offers while `marker` is not `null`, so keep paging until it is `null`. An unknown account answers 404 `not-found`. An answer is fresh for 10 seconds, or 4 seconds when an offer has an `Expiration`, the policy of its latest-ledger read.

When to use: To see which DEX offers an account has open and whether each can still execute: before cancelling or replacing offers, or to check how much of an account's open offers its balances back.

When not to use: To read the order book of a pair (use `/v1/xrpl/orderbook`) or estimate the cost of a trade (use `/v1/xrpl/slippage`); for the account's balances and trust lines, use `/v1/xrpl/account/{address}/summary` or `/v1/xrpl/account/{address}/lines`.

get.summary: An account's escrows, payment channels and checks by direction, its deposit preauthorizations, tickets and owner reserve, and what blocks deleting it.
get.description:
Aggregates what the account has committed on the validated ledger, without listing the objects. The route reads up to 3 pages of 400 of the account's ledger objects (`account_objects` with no type filter; the later pages on the ledger of the first one) and the account entry; when the account owns more, or a later page fails, `truncated` is `true` and the counts cover the pages read. Escrows, payment channels and checks are split by direction: `out` when the account is the source, `in` when it is the destination (an escrow to the account itself counts as `out` only). Escrows report `count`, `asset_totals` per asset as `{asset, value}` (XRP in XRP, not drops; a 40-hex currency code also carries `currency_ascii`; an MPT sum is `{asset, value: null, value_atomic}`, its exact base units in `value_atomic` and `value` null because this route reads no issuance), `next_release_at` (the earliest `FinishAfter` not yet passed, conditional escrows included, ISO 8601 UTC), `finishable_now` (no `Condition`, the validated ledger close time strictly after `FinishAfter` and not after `CancelAfter`) and `cancelable_now` (the close time strictly after `CancelAfter`). Payment channels report `count`, `remaining_xrp` (`Amount` minus `Balance`, the XRP not yet paid out) and `closing_within_24h` (the earlier of `Expiration` and `CancelAfter` after the close time and at most 24 hours after it; an expired channel is not counted). Checks report `count`, `asset_totals` (the sum of the checks' `SendMax` per asset, expired checks included, in the shape and order of the escrows' `asset_totals`), `expired_count` (`Expiration` at or before the close time) and `expiring_within_24h` (after the close time and at most 24 hours after it). `deposit_preauths` counts the account's DepositPreauth entries `by_account` and `by_credentials`; `tickets` is the account's `TicketCount`, exact even when the scan is truncated; `owner_reserve_xrp` is `OwnerCount` times the live owner reserve increment. `deletion_blockers` counts per `account_objects` type (keys in alphabetical order, only the types present) the owned entries that block AccountDelete: every type except `offer`, `signer_list`, `ticket`, `deposit_preauth`, `nft_offer`, `did`, `oracle`, `credential` and `delegate`, which the ledger deletes with the account, so a trust line (`state`) or an NFT page (`nft_page`) counts, and so does a type the route does not recognize. `lower_bound` is `true` when `truncated`. A `total` of 0 alone does not make the account deletable: its sequence age, the number of objects it owns, the NFTs it minted, the fee and the destination's own rules also decide. The route reads the reserves only when the account owns objects, and the latest validated ledger only when an escrow, check or channel has a time field. Each failed read is named in `checks_failed` (`objects` for a later page, `account`, `reserves`, `ledger`) and leaves the fields that need it `null`; a failed `ledger` read leaves a time-based figure `null` only in a direction that holds an object with the time field that figure reads. An unknown account answers 404 `not-found`. An answer is fresh for 10 seconds, or 4 seconds when it reads the latest validated ledger, the policy of that read.

When to use: Before deleting or winding down an account: to see which escrows can be finished or cancelled now, how much XRP is left in its payment channels, which checks expire soon, how much XRP its owned objects lock in reserve, and which owned entries block AccountDelete.

When not to use: To list the open DEX offers and how funded each one is (use `/v1/xrpl/account/{address}/offers`) or the trust lines (use `/v1/xrpl/account/{address}/lines`); for the balance and owner count, use `/v1/xrpl/account/{address}/summary`.
