get.summary: Is this account a member of this XRPL permissioned domain, as its owner or through an accepted, unexpired credential?
get.description:
Reads the PermissionedDomain `domain_id` from the validated ledger with one `ledger_entry` call, then each credential the domain accepts with `account` as its subject, the owner included (one `ledger_entry` call each, in parallel), together with the latest validated ledger, whose close time decides expiry. The answer echoes `domain_id`, in the upper-case hex the route reads, and `account`. Each row of `credentials` has a `status`: `missing` (the account holds no such credential), `expired` (its `Expiration` is before the validated ledger close time; one equal to the close time is still valid), `not_accepted` (the account has not accepted it), `valid`, or `unknown` (its read failed, or it has an `Expiration` and the close time could not be read). An expired credential is `expired` even when it is not accepted. Each verdict answers its own uses and is `eligible`, `not_eligible` or `unknown`. `credential_verdict` judges the account's credentials against the domain, for MPT `DomainID` authorization and private vault deposits, with no owner exemption: `eligible` when any credential is `valid`, `unknown` when none is valid and any is `unknown`, else `not_eligible`. Two protocol uses add their own rules: the owner of a private vault deposits into it without a domain check, and an account that already holds an MPToken passes MPT authorization even when `validDomain` fails. `dex_verdict` is membership for trading in the domain's permissioned order books: the owner is `eligible` with `dex_membership: "owner"` whatever its credentials; any other account takes its `credential_verdict`, with `dex_membership: "credential"` when `eligible`, else `null`. Each `unknown` credential is named in `checks_failed` as `credential:<issuer>:<credential_type>`. `matched_credential` is the first `valid` credential in the domain's order, the owner's included; `null` when none is valid. The rows of `credentials` and `matched_credential` also carry the credential's `expires_at` (its `Expiration`, ISO 8601 UTC, `null` without one) and `uri` (its `URI`, hex as the ledger stores it, `null` when absent), both `null` when the credential is missing or its read failed. Each found credential carries its `credential_id`, its ledger entry index, which `/v1/xrpl/payment-readiness` takes in `credentials`. `credential_type` is in ledger hex; `credential_type_ascii` is its text when every byte is printable ASCII, else `null`. A missing domain answers 404 `not-found`. Every answer, the owner's included, is fresh for 4 seconds, the policy of its latest-ledger read.

When to use: Before trading in a permissioned order book (`/v1/xrpl/orderbook` or `/v1/xrpl/slippage` with `domain`): to check whether an account is a member of the domain, as its owner or through an accepted, unexpired credential, and which credential qualifies it.

When not to use: To check whether one payment can succeed now (use `/v1/xrpl/payment-readiness`, whose `credentials` takes the `credential_id` values of this answer), or to read the permissioned order book itself (use `/v1/xrpl/orderbook` with `domain`). get.summary: One page of an account's open DEX offers, with how funded each one is.
get.description:
Returns one page of the account's open DEX offers from the validated ledger, in the ledger's order. Each offer has `seq` (the sequence number of the transaction that created it), `sells` (TakerGets) and `buys` (TakerPays) as `{asset, value}` (XRP in XRP, not drops; a 40-hex currency code also carries `currency_ascii`; an MPT one is `{asset, value: null, value_atomic}`, its exact base units in `value_atomic` and `value` null because this route reads no issuance), `price` (buys / sells, an MPT side in its base units, `null` when `sells` is zero), `funded_ratio`, `expires_at` (ISO 8601 UTC, `null` without an `Expiration`), `expired` (`true` when the `Expiration` is at or before the validated ledger close time) and the offer flags `passive`, `sell` and `hybrid` (`lsfHybrid`: the offer sits in a permissioned domain's book and in the open book). `funded_ratio` is min(1, available / `sells`), computed for each offer on its own, so offers that share a balance are not netted: available is the spendable XRP (the balance minus the reserve, never below 0) for an offer selling XRP, and for a token the trust line balance (a negative one counts as 0) divided by the issuer's TransferRate / 1e9. It is `1` when the account issues the token it sells, and `0` when the issuer froze the line or all its tokens, when the lines page is complete and holds no line for the token, or when the line of the token the offer buys is deep-frozen by its issuer. It is `null` for an MPT, when the line of the token it sells or buys may lie beyond the 400-line page the route reads, for the offers selling tokens of issuers beyond the first 10 distinct issuers of the page, and when a read it needs failed. Each failed read is named in `checks_failed` (`account`, `lines`, `issuer:<address>`, `ledger`, `reserves`); a failed `ledger` read leaves `expired` `null` for the offers with an `Expiration`. `totals` counts the offers of this page (`offer_count`) and the `unfunded` ones (`funded_ratio` `0`). Besides the page, the route reads only what its offers need: the account entry and the reserves when an offer sells XRP, one page of up to 400 trust lines when an offer sells or buys a token the account does not issue, the account entry of the issuer of each such token an offer sells, and the latest validated ledger when an offer has an `Expiration`. `limit` is 10 to 50 offers (default 20), and `marker` is an opaque cursor: send it back unchanged to get the next page; it is `null` on the last page and only valid for the address that produced it. A page can hold fewer than `limit` offers while `marker` is not `null`, so keep paging until it is `null`. An unknown account answers 404 `not-found`. An answer is fresh for 10 seconds, or 4 seconds when an offer has an `Expiration`, the policy of its latest-ledger read.

When to use: To see which DEX offers an account has open and whether each can still execute: before cancelling or replacing offers, or to check how much of an account's open offers its balances back.

When not to use: To read the order book of a pair (use `/v1/xrpl/orderbook`) or estimate the cost of a trade (use `/v1/xrpl/slippage`); for the account's balances and trust lines, use `/v1/xrpl/account/{address}/summary` or `/v1/xrpl/account/{address}/lines`. Per call: 0.0363 EUR at the default regime. With prepaid credits, debit per call: 0.03 EUR-denominated units (approx 33 calls per bundle) or 0.036 USD-denominated units (approx 22 calls per bundle).

get.summary: An account's escrows, payment channels and checks by direction, its deposit preauthorizations, tickets and owner reserve, and what blocks deleting it.
get.description:
Aggregates what the account has committed on the validated ledger, without listing the objects. The route reads up to 3 pages of 400 of the account's ledger objects (`account_objects` with no type filter; the later pages on the ledger of the first one) and the account entry; when the account owns more, or a later page fails, `truncated` is `true` and the counts cover the pages read. Escrows, payment channels and checks are split by direction: `out` when the account is the source, `in` when it is the destination (an escrow to the account itself counts as `out` only). Escrows report `count`, `asset_totals` per asset as `{asset, value}` (XRP in XRP, not drops; a 40-hex currency code also carries `currency_ascii`; an MPT sum is `{asset, value: null, value_atomic}`, its exact base units in `value_atomic` and `value` null because this route reads no issuance), `next_release_at` (the earliest `FinishAfter` not yet passed, conditional escrows included, ISO 8601 UTC), `finishable_now` (no `Condition`, the validated ledger close time strictly after `FinishAfter` and not after `CancelAfter`) and `cancelable_now` (the close time strictly after `CancelAfter`). Payment channels report `count`, `remaining_xrp` (`Amount` minus `Balance`, the XRP not yet paid out) and `closing_within_24h` (the earlier of `Expiration` and `CancelAfter` after the close time and at most 24 hours after it; an expired channel is not counted). Checks report `count`, `asset_totals` (the sum of the checks' `SendMax` per asset, expired checks included, in the shape and order of the escrows' `asset_totals`), `expired_count` (`Expiration` at or before the close time) and `expiring_within_24h` (after the close time and at most 24 hours after it). `deposit_preauths` counts the account's DepositPreauth entries `by_account` and `by_credentials`; `tickets` is the account's `TicketCount`, exact even when the scan is truncated; `owner_reserve_xrp` is `OwnerCount` times the live owner reserve increment. `deletion_blockers` counts per `account_objects` type (keys in alphabetical order, only the types present) the owned entries that block AccountDelete: every type except `offer`, `signer_list`, `ticket`, `deposit_preauth`, `nft_offer`, `did`, `oracle`, `credential` and `delegate`, which the ledger deletes with the account, so a trust line (`state`) or an NFT page (`nft_page`) counts, and so does a type the route does not recognize. `lower_bound` is `true` when `truncated`. A `total` of 0 alone does not make the account deletable: its sequence age, the number of objects it owns, the NFTs it minted, the fee and the destination's own rules also decide. The route reads the reserves only when the account owns objects, and the latest validated ledger only when an escrow, check or channel has a time field. Each failed read is named in `checks_failed` (`objects` for a later page, `account`, `reserves`, `ledger`) and leaves the fields that need it `null`; a failed `ledger` read leaves a time-based figure `null` only in a direction that holds an object with the time field that figure reads. An unknown account answers 404 `not-found`. An answer is fresh for 10 seconds, or 4 seconds when it reads the latest validated ledger, the policy of that read.

When to use: Before deleting or winding down an account: to see which escrows can be finished or cancelled now, how much XRP is left in its payment channels, which checks expire soon, how much XRP its owned objects lock in reserve, and which owned entries block AccountDelete.

When not to use: To list the open DEX offers and how funded each one is (use `/v1/xrpl/account/{address}/offers`) or the trust lines (use `/v1/xrpl/account/{address}/lines`); for the balance and owner count, use `/v1/xrpl/account/{address}/summary`. Per call: 0.0242 EUR at the default regime. With prepaid credits, debit per call: 0.02 EUR-denominated units (approx 50 calls per bundle) or 0.024 USD-denominated units (approx 34 calls per bundle).

get.summary: Buy or sell pressure of a pair's funded order book: a score from 0 to 100 and its band, from the depth near mid.
get.description:
Reads the funded order book of `base`/`quote` (up to 100 levels per side, both sides from one validated ledger: the same cached book as `/v1/xrpl/orderbook` at depth 100) and reports `best_bid` and `best_ask`, the prices of the best funded bid and ask (quote per base, as `/v1/xrpl/orderbook` names them; each `null` when its side is empty), then the figures computed from them: `mid` = (best_bid + best_ask) / 2 (quote per base), `spread_bps` = (best_ask − best_bid) / mid × 10000 and `bands`: for 10, 50 and 100 bps around `mid`, the funded base quantity of the bids (`bid_depth`) and of the asks (`ask_depth`) priced within the band, bounds included, and their `imbalance_ratio` = (bid_depth − ask_depth) / (bid_depth + ask_depth), from -1 (asks only) to 1 (bids only), `null` when both depths are 0. The body opens with `base` and `quote`, the queried pair in the canonical form the route reads, each with its readable text for a 40-hex code. `score` = 50 × (1 + imbalance_ratio_50), rounded half-up to an integer from 0 to 100, where imbalance_ratio_50 is the unrounded `imbalance_ratio` of the 50 bps band. `band` is decided on that integer score: `sell_pressure` below 40, `balanced` from 40 to 60 inclusive and `buy_pressure` above 60. A one-sided book gives `mid`, `spread_bps`, `bands`, `score` and `band` `null` with the reason `one_sided_book`, and keeps the best price of its non-empty side; a two-sided book with no funded depth within 50 bps of `mid` gives `score` and `band` `null` with `no_depth_within_band`. The AMM is not used. `baseline` compares this book with its stored 7-day series: 15-minute snapshots of the books of the registry stablecoins paired with XRP and with each other, read from one dedicated upstream, each without the offers expired at the close time of its ledger, each orientation stored on its own (depth in its base), so `base`/`quote` is compared with the series of that same order. Its seven figures, in this order, are `spread_bps`, `depth_bid_10`, `depth_ask_10`, `depth_bid_50`, `depth_ask_50`, `depth_bid_100` and `depth_ask_100`, each with its stored `points` in the window of the 672 15-minute slots ending at the latest recorded slot, `gaps` (672 − points, the slots with no stored point), `median`, `mean` and `stddev` (the mean and the population standard deviation of the stored values, over the stored points), `live` and `zscore` = (live − mean) / population standard deviation of the stored values, rounded half-up to 2 decimals (`null` when that deviation is 0), where `live` is the same figure of this book: the depths as `bands` reports them (`depth_bid_50` is the `bid_depth` of the 50 bps band) and `spread_bps` before its rounding to 2 decimals. A one-sided book has no live figure: every `live` and `zscore` is `null` and the stored statistics are kept. A figure with fewer than 288 stored slots (3 days) is warming up: its `median`, `mean`, `stddev` and `zscore` are `null`, its `live` is still served, and `reasons` contains `warming_up`; `baseline` is `null` while every figure warms up. A pair outside that list, and every pair while the book series is not tracked, has `baseline: null` with `not_tracked`; a stored series that cannot be read, or that lacks a figure, gives `baseline: null` with `baseline_unavailable`; the score, its band and every other figure are still served and never depend on the baseline. `reasons` lists the score's own reason first, then at most one of `warming_up`, `not_tracked` and `baseline_unavailable`, and is empty when none applies. As on `/v1/xrpl/orderbook`, offers whose expiry is at or before the close time of the latest validated ledger are left out of the book, possibly slightly early, and a close time that cannot be read fails the answer (503 `upstream-unavailable`). `meta` describes the book read and that latest-ledger read; the 7-day summary of the stored series is computed once per 15-minute slot, from the 672 slots ending at the latest recorded slot, and cached until that slot ends (a request made before the current slot is recorded gets the previous slot's summary). The score, its band and the z-scores are defined computations over the book and the stored series, not advice. Bps fields are decimal strings rounded half-up to 2 decimals; prices, depths, imbalance ratios and medians are decimal strings, and z-scores decimal strings rounded half-up to 2 decimals. An answer is fresh for 4 seconds, the policy of the order book it reads.

When to use: To measure how the funded depth near mid of a pair's order book is split between bids and asks, as one score with its band.

When not to use: To read the order book levels (use `/v1/xrpl/orderbook`), the cost of a trade of a given size, CLOB against AMM (use `/v1/xrpl/slippage`), or an AMM pool (use `/v1/xrpl/amm/{a}/{b}`). Per call: 0.0121 EUR at the default regime. With prepaid credits, debit per call: 0.0025 EUR-denominated units (approx 400 calls per bundle) or 0.003 USD-denominated units (approx 273 calls per bundle).

get.summary: How far a registry stablecoin trades from its peg on the XRP Ledger DEX: the deviation of each price route, their median and a status.
get.description:
Prices `asset`, an XRPL stablecoin of the registry that `/v1/xrpl/stablecoin/{asset}` checks (RLUSD, USDC or EURØP), in `against`, a USD stablecoin of the registry other than `asset`. Without `against` the route uses the peg default: the other USD registry coin for a USD asset (USDC for RLUSD, RLUSD for USDC) and RLUSD for an EUR asset. Any other `asset` or `against` answers 400 naming that field, with no ledger read. `asset` and `against` are answered as `CODE.issuer` with the 40-hex code. `expected_price` is the price on peg: `1` for a USD asset, and for an EUR asset the stored ECB reference rate in USD per EUR, the latest on or before the answer's UTC date. The routes come from the validated ledger only: `clob_direct` is the mid of the direct order book (base `asset`, quote `against`), `amm_direct` the fee-free spot of the direct AMM pool (a frozen or empty pool counts as no pool), and `via_xrp` the mid of XRP in `against` divided by the mid of XRP in `asset`. `routes` lists only the available ones, each with its `observed_price` and its `deviation_bps` = (observed_price / expected_price − 1) × 10000. The headline `deviation_bps` is the median of the unrounded route deviations (the mean of the two middle values for an even count), rounded half-up to 2 decimals. `status` is decided on that reported headline: `on_peg` when |deviation_bps| ≤ 50, `drifting` when 50 < |deviation_bps| ≤ 200, `off_peg` when |deviation_bps| > 200, and `unknown` without a route (`routes` is then empty and `deviation_bps` `null`). `bid_depth_at_peg_50` is the funded quantity of `asset` bid in the direct book priced in the closed interval [expected_price × (1 − 0.005), expected_price × (1 + 0.005)], that is within 50 bps of `expected_price`, bounds included: the demand that holds the peg; `ask_depth_at_peg_50` is the funded quantity of `asset` offered in the same interval, the supply that pushes it down; and `depth_at_peg_50` = bid_depth_at_peg_50 + ask_depth_at_peg_50, both sides together. `reference_rate` is the ECB rate an EUR asset is measured against (`rate_date`, `usd_per_eur`, `age_days` and `data_source`), and `null` for a USD asset; an EUR asset without a stored rate gives `expected_price`, every `deviation_bps`, `bid_depth_at_peg_50`, `ask_depth_at_peg_50`, `depth_at_peg_50` and `reference_rate` `null` and `status` `unknown`. `baseline` compares the direct book (base `asset`, quote `against`) with its stored 7-day series: 15-minute snapshots of the books of the registry stablecoins paired with XRP and with each other, read from one dedicated upstream, each without the offers expired at the close time of its ledger, each orientation stored on its own (depth in its base); every pair this route accepts is in that list, in its own order. Its seven figures, in this order, are `spread_bps`, `depth_bid_10`, `depth_ask_10`, `depth_bid_50`, `depth_ask_50`, `depth_bid_100` and `depth_ask_100`, each with its stored `points` in the window of the 672 15-minute slots ending at the latest recorded slot, `gaps` (672 − points, the slots with no stored point), `median`, `mean` and `stddev` (the mean and the population standard deviation of the stored values, over the stored points), `live` and `zscore` = (live − mean) / population standard deviation of the stored values, rounded half-up to 2 decimals (`null` when that deviation is 0), where `live` is the same statistic of the direct book read here: its spread / mid × 10000, not rounded to 2 decimals, and the funded base quantity of its bids and of its asks priced within 10, 50 and 100 bps of its mid, bounds included, as `/v1/xrpl/metrics/pressure` computes them (around the mid, not around `expected_price`). A one-sided direct book has no live figure: every `live` and `zscore` is `null` and the stored statistics are kept. A figure with fewer than 288 stored slots (3 days) is warming up: its `median`, `mean`, `stddev` and `zscore` are `null`, its `live` is still served, and `reasons` contains `warming_up`; `baseline` is `null` while every figure warms up. Every pair has `baseline: null` with `not_tracked` while the book series is not tracked; a stored series that cannot be read, or that lacks a figure, gives `baseline: null` with `baseline_unavailable`; every other field is still served and never depends on the baseline. `reasons` holds only the baseline reasons: at most one of `warming_up`, `not_tracked` and `baseline_unavailable`, and is empty when none applies. As on `/v1/xrpl/orderbook`, offers whose expiry is at or before the close time of the latest validated ledger are left out of every book, possibly slightly early, and a close time that cannot be read fails the answer (503 `upstream-unavailable`). The books are read at depth 100 (the same cached books as `/v1/xrpl/orderbook`) and the pool through the same cache entry as `/v1/xrpl/amm/{a}/{b}`; `meta` reports the lowest ledger, the oldest read and the worst cache state of these reads and of that latest-ledger read, the ECB rate and the stored series not included; the 7-day summary of the stored series is computed once per 15-minute slot, from the 672 slots ending at the latest recorded slot, and cached until that slot ends (a request made before the current slot is recorded gets the previous slot's summary). An AMM read that fails for another reason than a missing pool fails the answer as a failed book read does (503 `upstream-unavailable` when no node can serve it). The deviations, the status and the z-scores are defined computations over the ledger and the stored series, not advice. Bps fields are decimal strings rounded half-up to 2 decimals; prices, quantities and medians are decimal strings, and z-scores decimal strings rounded half-up to 2 decimals. An answer is fresh for 4 seconds, the shortest policy of its reads.

When to use: To check, from the XRP Ledger's own order books and AMM pools, how far a registry stablecoin trades from its peg against another registry coin, and how much funded depth sits near the peg.

When not to use: To check that an issued currency is the canonical registry coin, or to read its issuer posture (use `/v1/xrpl/stablecoin/{asset}`); for an asset outside the registry, which this route refuses, read its order book (`/v1/xrpl/orderbook`) or its AMM pool (`/v1/xrpl/amm/{a}/{b}`). Per call: 0.0363 EUR at the default regime. With prepaid credits, debit per call: 0.03 EUR-denominated units (approx 33 calls per bundle) or 0.036 USD-denominated units (approx 22 calls per bundle).

get.summary: The EUR/USD rate the XRP Ledger DEX implies through the EUR registry stablecoin against each USD registry stablecoin, and its basis to the ECB reference rate.
get.description:
Prices EURØP, the EUR stablecoin of the registry that `/v1/xrpl/stablecoin/{asset}` checks, in each USD stablecoin of the registry, one leg per coin in registry order (RLUSD, then USDC), through the routes of `/v1/xrpl/metrics/peg`: `clob_direct` is the mid of the direct order book (base EURØP, quote the leg's USD coin), `amm_direct` the fee-free spot of the direct AMM pool (a frozen or empty pool counts as no pool), and `via_xrp` the mid of XRP in the USD coin divided by the mid of XRP in EURØP. Each leg lists only its available `routes`, each with its `observed_price`, the USD per EUR it implies, and its `deviation_bps` = (observed_price / usd_per_eur − 1) × 10000, where usd_per_eur is the ECB reference rate; `implied_usd_per_eur` is the median of the unrounded `observed_price` values (the mean of the two middle values for an even count), and `basis_bps` = (implied_usd_per_eur / usd_per_eur − 1) × 10000, computed from the unrounded implied rate. `usd_leg_spread_bps` is the RLUSD leg's basis minus the USDC leg's, from the unrounded bases, and `null` unless both legs have a basis. A leg with no route has `routes` empty and `implied_usd_per_eur` and `basis_bps` `null`, and `reasons` holds `no_route`. `reference_rate` is the stored ECB reference rate in USD per EUR, the latest on or before the answer's UTC date (`rate_date`, `usd_per_eur`, `age_days` and `data_source`); without a stored rate `reference_rate`, every `deviation_bps`, `basis_bps` and `usd_leg_spread_bps` are `null` and `reasons` holds `reference_rate_unavailable`, while `implied_usd_per_eur` is still reported. `age_days` is the number of whole days from `rate_date` to the answer's UTC date, and `warnings` holds `stale_reference` when `age_days` is above 4 days (a rate 4 days old is not stale, one 5 days old is). Source: ECB statistics. The route takes no parameters. As on `/v1/xrpl/orderbook`, offers whose expiry is at or before the close time of the latest validated ledger are left out of every book, possibly slightly early, and a close time that cannot be read fails the answer (503 `upstream-unavailable`). The XRP/EURØP book both legs use is read once; the books are read at depth 100 (the same cached books as `/v1/xrpl/orderbook`) and the pools through the same cache entries as `/v1/xrpl/amm/{a}/{b}`; `meta` reports the lowest ledger, the oldest read and the worst cache state of these reads and of that latest-ledger read, the ECB rate not included. An AMM read that fails for another reason than a missing pool fails the answer as a failed book read does (503 `upstream-unavailable` when no node can serve it). The bases are defined computations over the ledger and the ECB rate, not advice. Bps fields are decimal strings rounded half-up to 2 decimals; prices are decimal strings. An answer is fresh for 4 seconds, the shortest policy of its reads.

When to use: To measure, from the XRP Ledger's own order books and AMM pools, the EUR/USD rate the DEX implies through the EUR registry stablecoin against each USD registry stablecoin, and how far it sits from the ECB reference rate.

When not to use: To measure how far one registry stablecoin trades from its peg against another registry coin (use `/v1/xrpl/metrics/peg`), or to read an order book or an AMM pool (use `/v1/xrpl/orderbook` or `/v1/xrpl/amm/{a}/{b}`). Per call: 0.0605 EUR at the default regime. With prepaid credits, debit per call: 0.05 EUR-denominated units (approx 20 calls per bundle) or 0.06 USD-denominated units (approx 13 calls per bundle).

get.summary: Whether a pair's AMM pool and its order book are apart after the AMM fee: per direction the gap, the executable size and the profit after transfer fees.
get.description:
Compares the AMM pool of `base`/`quote` with the pair's funded order book (up to 100 levels per side, both sides from one validated ledger: the same cached book as `/v1/xrpl/orderbook` at depth 100). Any pair is accepted; `quote` equal to `base` answers 400. The body opens with `base` and `quote`, the queried pair in the canonical form the route reads, each with its readable text for a 40-hex code. The inputs of both gaps follow: `amm_spot_price`, the pool's fee-free spot (quote reserve / base reserve) in quote per base, and `trading_fee_pct`, its trading fee in percent (TradingFee / 1000, as `/v1/xrpl/amm/{a}/{b}` gives it), both `null` without a usable pool (none, frozen or empty). `amm_to_clob` buys `base` on the pool and sells it into the bids, and `clob_to_amm` buys `base` from the asks and sells it into the pool. Each direction reports its book side's best price (`best_bid` for `amm_to_clob`, `best_ask` for `clob_to_amm`, quote per base, `null` when that side is empty); `gap_bps`, the gap in bps between that best price and the pool's price after its trading fee; `executable_base`, the base quantity tradable against the book; and `net_quote_profit`, the quote profit of that size after the issuers' transfer fees and before the XRP transaction costs of the legs, `null` when a transfer rate cannot be read. With B and Q the pool's base and quote reserves, spot = Q / B its fee-free price in quote per base and f its trading fee as a decimal fraction (the `trading_fee_pct` of `/v1/xrpl/amm/{a}/{b}` divided by 100: `0.5` there is f = 0.005), `amm_to_clob` has `gap_bps` = (best_bid − spot / (1 − f)) / (spot / (1 − f)) × 10000 and `clob_to_amm` has `gap_bps` = (spot × (1 − f) − best_ask) / best_ask × 10000, rounded half-up to 2 decimals. `status` is `open` when that reported `gap_bps` is above 0 and `no_opportunity` otherwise, so a gap below 0.005 bps is `no_opportunity`. For an open direction, `executable_base` comes from a walk of the book levels (the bids for `amm_to_clob`, the asks for `clob_to_amm`, best price first) against the closed-form marginal price of the pool, Q × B / ((B − x)² × (1 − f)) after buying x base from it and Q × B × (1 − f) / (B + y × (1 − f))² after selling y base into it: each level is taken until that marginal price reaches the level price, a level partly up to the size where it does, and the walk stops at equality. `net_quote_profit` follows the transfer-fee rule of an OfferCreate taker: the taker pays the transfer fee of the asset it sends, at its issuer's TransferRate / 1e9 (1e9, no fee, for XRP and for an issuer without a TransferRate), and the pool never pays one: the quote it sends costs it that amount × rate(quote) / 1e9, and the base it sends reaches the bids or the pool as that amount ÷ (rate(base) / 1e9). So `amm_to_clob` gives Σ(take × bid price) − Q × x / ((B − x) × (1 − f)) × rate(quote) / 1e9, the bids filled with x ÷ (rate(base) / 1e9), and `clob_to_amm` gives Q × y′ × (1 − f) / (B + y′ × (1 − f)) − Σ(take × ask price) × rate(quote) / 1e9, with y′ = y ÷ (rate(base) / 1e9) the base the pool receives; x or y is the `executable_base`, and rate(base) and rate(quote) are the TransferRate of each asset's issuer. A direction that is not open reports `executable_base` and `net_quote_profit` `"0"`, and one that cannot be evaluated (no pool, a frozen or empty pool, or the needed book side empty) also has `gap_bps` `null`. With `include_triangles=true` the answer adds `triangles`: the cycles XRP → RLUSD → USDC → XRP and XRP → USDC → RLUSD → XRP over the USD stablecoins of the registry, each with its `path`, its `legs`, `gap_bps` and `top_size_xrp`, the last two `null` when a leg's book side is empty or a transfer rate cannot be read. `legs` lists the three legs in cycle order, each with `input_asset` and `output_asset` (`XRP` or `CODE.issuer`, each with its readable text for a 40-hex code) and `price_after_fees`, its fee-inclusive leg rate in output per input, `null` when that leg's book side is empty or its transfer rate cannot be read. Each leg sells its input asset into the bids of the book with that asset as base, at the fee-inclusive leg rate best_bid ÷ (TransferRate / 1e9), with the TransferRate of the input asset's issuer (1e9 for XRP); `gap_bps` = (the product of the leg rates − 1) × 10000, and `top_size_xrp` is the XRP input that fills the smallest first bid level of the legs: each leg's first bid level `gets`, in its input asset, is grossed up by that asset's TransferRate / 1e9 (1e9 for XRP) and divided by the product of the preceding leg rates to carry it back to XRP, and the smallest result is reported. Without `include_triangles`, or with `false`, no triangle book is read and `triangles` is absent; any other value answers 400. As on `/v1/xrpl/orderbook`, offers whose expiry is at or before the close time of the latest validated ledger are left out of every book, possibly slightly early, and a close time that cannot be read fails the answer (503 `upstream-unavailable`). The triangle books are read at depth 100 through the same cached books, the pool through the same cache entry as `/v1/xrpl/amm/{a}/{b}` and the transfer rates through the issuers' cached TransferRate; `meta` reports the lowest ledger, the oldest read and the worst cache state of the books, the pool and that latest-ledger read, the transfer rates not included. A failed book read, a failed triangle book read or an AMM read that fails for another reason than a missing pool fails the answer (503 `upstream-unavailable` when no node can serve it). The gaps, sizes and profits are defined computations over the ledger, not advice and not an executable quote. Bps fields are decimal strings rounded half-up to 2 decimals; quantities are decimal strings. An answer is fresh for 4 seconds, the shortest policy of its reads.

When to use: To find whether a pair's AMM pool and its funded order book are apart after the AMM fee, in which direction, how much base the gap allows and the profit after transfer fees, optionally with the cycles of the USD registry stablecoins via XRP.

When not to use: To estimate the cost of a trade of a given size, CLOB against AMM (use `/v1/xrpl/slippage`), or to read the order book levels (use `/v1/xrpl/orderbook`) or an AMM pool (use `/v1/xrpl/amm/{a}/{b}`); the answer measures the ledger and is not an executable quote. Per call: 0.0363 EUR at the default regime. With prepaid credits, debit per call: 0.03 EUR-denominated units (approx 33 calls per bundle) or 0.036 USD-denominated units (approx 22 calls per bundle).

get.summary: How stressed a registry stablecoin's liquidity is against its peg default: a score from 0 to 100, its band and the four weighted components behind it.
get.description:
Measures how stressed the liquidity of `asset` is against its peg default. `asset` is an XRPL stablecoin of the registry that `/v1/xrpl/stablecoin/{asset}` checks (RLUSD, USDC or EURØP), and its peg default is the other USD registry coin for a USD asset (USDC for RLUSD, RLUSD for USDC) and RLUSD for an EUR asset. Any other `asset` answers 400 naming it, with no ledger read. The route reads what `/v1/xrpl/metrics/peg` reads for that pair, plus the issuer's account. The body opens with `asset`, the queried stablecoin in the canonical form the route reads, with its readable text for a 40-hex code. `components` lists four weighted components, each with its `value_ratio` from 0 to 1, its integer `weight` and its `contribution` = weight × value_ratio; `weight` and `contribution` are in score points, the unit of `score`. The weights are `peg` 40, `spread` 20, `depth` 25 and `amm_gap` 15, summing to 100, the range of `score`. Each value is clamped to [0, 1]: `peg` = |deviation_bps| / 200, from peg's unrounded headline `deviation_bps`; `spread` = spread_bps / 100, from the direct book's unrounded `spread_bps`; `depth` = 1 − depth_at_peg_50 / 100000, from peg's unrounded `depth_at_peg_50` in units of `asset` (more depth near the peg means less stress); and `amm_gap` = |amm_clob_gap_bps| / 100, where amm_clob_gap_bps = (amm_spot − clob_mid) / clob_mid × 10000 between the direct AMM pool's fee-free spot and the direct book's mid, 0 without a pool (a frozen or empty pool counts as no pool). A component whose input is missing (a one-sided direct book has no spread and no mid; an EUR asset without a stored ECB rate has no deviation and no depth at peg) has `value_ratio` 1 and counts its full weight. Each component states its raw input right after `name`: `input_bps` for `peg`, `spread` and `amm_gap` (deviation_bps, spread_bps or amm_clob_gap_bps, signed, before the absolute value and the clamp, rounded half-up to 2 decimals) and `input_depth` for `depth` (depth_at_peg_50, in units of `asset`), each `null` where it does not apply or when the input is missing, and `input_missing`, `true` when the input is missing, so a missing input never reads like a maxed one; without a pool `amm_gap` is 0 by rule, not missing (`input_bps` `null`, `input_missing` `false`). `score` is the sum of the unrounded contributions rounded half-up to an integer from 0 to 100, and `band` is decided on that integer score: `low` below 25, `elevated` from 25 to below 50, `high` from 50 to below 75 and `severe` from 75. An issuer global freeze gives `score` 100 and `band` `severe` with the reason `issuer_global_freeze`, and never `no_route`, even without a route; without a freeze and without a route between the asset and its peg default `score` and `band` are `null` with `no_route`; the components are listed in both cases. `baseline` compares the direct book (base `asset`, quote its peg default) with its stored 7-day series: 15-minute snapshots of the books of the registry stablecoins paired with XRP and with each other, read from one dedicated upstream, each without the offers expired at the close time of its ledger, each orientation stored on its own (depth in its base); every pair this route reads is in that list, in its own order. Its seven figures, in this order, are `spread_bps`, `depth_bid_10`, `depth_ask_10`, `depth_bid_50`, `depth_ask_50`, `depth_bid_100` and `depth_ask_100`, each with its stored `points` in the window of the 672 15-minute slots ending at the latest recorded slot, `gaps` (672 − points, the slots with no stored point), `median`, `mean` and `stddev` (the mean and the population standard deviation of the stored values, over the stored points), `live` and `zscore` = (live − mean) / population standard deviation of the stored values, rounded half-up to 2 decimals (`null` when that deviation is 0), where `live` is the same statistic of the direct book read here: its spread / mid × 10000, not rounded to 2 decimals, and the funded base quantity of its bids and of its asks priced within 10, 50 and 100 bps of its mid, bounds included, as `/v1/xrpl/metrics/pressure` computes them (around the mid, not around the price on peg). A one-sided direct book has no live figure: every `live` and `zscore` is `null` and the stored statistics are kept. A figure with fewer than 288 stored slots (3 days) is warming up: its `median`, `mean`, `stddev` and `zscore` are `null`, its `live` is still served, and `reasons` contains `warming_up`; `baseline` is `null` while every figure warms up. Every pair has `baseline: null` with `not_tracked` while the book series is not tracked; a stored series that cannot be read, or that lacks a figure, gives `baseline: null` with `baseline_unavailable`; the score, its band and the components are still served and never depend on the baseline. `reasons` lists `issuer_global_freeze` or `no_route` first, then at most one of `warming_up`, `not_tracked` and `baseline_unavailable`, so a global freeze while the book series is not tracked answers `["issuer_global_freeze", "not_tracked"]`, and is empty when none applies. For an EUR asset the price on peg is the stored ECB reference rate in USD per EUR, the latest on or before the answer's UTC date. As on `/v1/xrpl/orderbook`, offers whose expiry is at or before the close time of the latest validated ledger are left out of every book, possibly slightly early; when that close time cannot be read, the books count as missing inputs and the answer is still served: `spread` and `depth` count their full weights with `input_missing` `true`, `amm_gap` too with a pool (the book has no mid), and `peg` is left with the pool's route only. The books are read at depth 100 (the same cached books as `/v1/xrpl/orderbook`), the pool through the same cache entry as `/v1/xrpl/amm/{a}/{b}` and the issuer through the same cached account entry as `/v1/xrpl/stablecoin/{asset}`; `meta` reports the lowest ledger, the oldest read and the worst cache state of these reads and of that latest-ledger read when it is used, the ECB rate and the stored series not included; the 7-day summary of the stored series is computed once per 15-minute slot, from the 672 slots ending at the latest recorded slot, and cached until that slot ends (a request made before the current slot is recorded gets the previous slot's summary). An issuer account that does not exist reads as no freeze; any other failed issuer or book read, or an AMM read that fails for another reason than a missing pool, fails the answer (503 `upstream-unavailable` when no node can serve it). The score, its band and the z-scores are defined computations over the ledger and the stored series, not advice. Value ratios, contributions and medians are decimal strings, and z-scores decimal strings rounded half-up to 2 decimals. An answer is fresh for 4 seconds, the shortest policy of its reads.

When to use: To score, from the XRP Ledger's own order books, AMM pool and issuer account, how stressed a registry stablecoin's liquidity is against its peg default, as one score with its band and the components behind it.

When not to use: To read the peg deviation of each price route (use `/v1/xrpl/metrics/peg`), or to check that an issued currency is the canonical registry coin and read its issuer posture (use `/v1/xrpl/stablecoin/{asset}`); for an asset outside the registry, which this route refuses, read its order book (`/v1/xrpl/orderbook`) or its AMM pool (`/v1/xrpl/amm/{a}/{b}`). Per call: 0.0363 EUR at the default regime. With prepaid credits, debit per call: 0.03 EUR-denominated units (approx 33 calls per bundle) or 0.036 USD-denominated units (approx 22 calls per bundle).

Standard codes are case-sensitive: `usd` and `USD` are different tokens, so send the exact code. A standard code uses letters, digits or `?!@#$%^&*<>(){}[]|` and is never `XRP`; percent-encode the symbols in a URL (for example `%3F` for `?`). get.summary: Will this Solana transfer succeed? A verdict for SOL or an SPL or Token-2022 token.
get.description:
Checks one planned transfer of SOL or of an SPL Token or Token-2022 token against finalized on-chain state and returns a `verdict` (`ready`, `not_ready` or `unknown`), every matched reason (blocking code) and warning code, `checks_failed`, and the derived figures: the amount in base units (`amount_atomic`), the source's balance of the asset that insufficient_balance compares (`source_balance`, `{asset, value, value_atomic}` in display and base units: the source token account's amount, or the source's lamports for SOL; zero when the source has no token account of the mint; for a source token account that cannot be decoded, its base-layout amount, or null without the 165-byte base), the token accounts the transfer debits and credits (`source_token_account` and `destination_token_account`, the derived associated token accounts, the destination's also when it must be created or another program's account holds its address; null for SOL), whether the destination token account must be created and the lamports to create it (its rent, or only the shortfall when its address already holds SOL), the Token-2022 transfer fee and the net amount in base units (`transfer_fee_atomic`, `net_amount_atomic`), plus `destination_kind` (the class of the destination account), the display fields `ui_multiplier` and `interest_rate_pct` (percent) of mints that scale their UI amount, and `transfer_fee_next` when a newer transfer fee is pending (its `transfer_fee_pct`, its `transfer_fee_max` in display units and its `epoch`). Reasons: insufficient_balance, insufficient_sol_for_fees (5,000 lamports for one signature, priority fees excluded, plus the lamports to create the destination token account when it is missing, only the shortfall when its address already holds SOL, plus the amount for SOL), source_below_rent_exempt, destination_below_rent_exempt, source_frozen, destination_frozen, non_transferable, mint_paused, destination_ata_occupied (an account owned by another program already holds the destination's token account address, so the token account cannot be created there), destination_frozen_on_creation (the mint's default account state would create the destination token account frozen), destination_not_wallet (the destination is a token account, mint, multisig, program, stake or vote account: pay its owner wallet), destination_ata_owner_mismatch (the account at the destination's token account address belongs to another owner), source_not_system_account (a SOL transfer from an account that is not a plain System wallet, such as a nonce account), destination_confidential_only (the destination token account refuses non-confidential credits). Warnings: destination_off_curve, memo_required, destination_program_owned (the destination is an account of kind `other`: owned by another program, or a System account with unexpected data), ui_amount_scaled (the mint scales its UI amount; `amount` stays raw / 10^decimals, and `ui_multiplier` and `interest_rate_pct` are for display only), transfer_fee_changing (a newer transfer fee starts at a later epoch; see `transfer_fee_next`). `verdict` is `not_ready` on any reason, else `unknown` on any failed check, else `ready`. `checks_failed` names source_token_account or destination_token_account when that token account exists but cannot be decoded (an SPL Token account of a length other than 165 bytes, a Token-2022 account under 165 bytes, a Token-2022 account of the multisig length of 355 bytes, a Token-2022 account type byte other than 2, a bad TLV, a ConfidentialTransferAccount of a size other than 295 bytes, or an account state byte other than 0 (uninitialized), 1 (initialized) or 2 (frozen)): its memo and confidential-credit state is then unknown, never read as absent, and an undecodable destination token account is never reported as missing; an undecodable source still gives insufficient_balance when the amount in its base layout is below the transfer amount. Any other failed read fails the whole request. The rent-exempt minimum is read live and never hardcoded. Every figure is read at finalized commitment, so it can lag the tip of the chain by about 13 seconds; `meta.slot` is the lowest context slot of the reads behind the answer. The amount is not part of any cache key, so the verdict is computed per request.

When to use: Before building or signing a Solana transfer, to learn whether it will fail and what it will cost in rent and fees.

When not to use: Not a simulation of the exact transaction (no priority fee, no program logic), not a token price or holder lookup, and not a way to read raw accounts.

get.summary: Is this Solana token safe to hold or receive? A safe, warn or danger verdict.
get.description:
Decodes an SPL Token or Token-2022 mint (including its extensions) and returns the token program, decimals, the exact supply in base units (`supply_atomic`) and in display units (`supply`, `supply_atomic` / 10^decimals, exact, not adjusted by a UI multiplier or interest rate), the authorities, the extension names, the transfer fee active at the current epoch (`transfer_fee_pct` in percent and `transfer_fee_max`, the maximum fee per transfer in display units of the mint, exact; both null without a TransferFeeConfig), the values of the extensions it decodes, each null without its extension (`transfer_fee_next`, the newer fee while its epoch is after the current epoch, with its `transfer_fee_pct`, its `transfer_fee_max` in display units and its `epoch`; `transfer_fee_authority`; `paused`; `default_account_state`, `initialized` or `frozen`; `interest_rate_pct`, an annual rate in percent compounded continuously; `ui_multiplier`, the ScaledUiAmount multiplier in effect; `ui_multiplier_next` and `ui_multiplier_next_at`, the new multiplier and its effective time while that time is after the response time (`ui_multiplier_next` null when the new multiplier is not a finite number, its time still served); `permanent_delegate`; `transfer_hook_program_id`; `mint_close_authority`; `metadata_address`; a key that is unset is null) and a `verdict` (`safe`, `warn` or `danger`) with every matched reason code. `danger`: permanent_delegate, transfer_hook, pausable, default_account_frozen. `warn`: mint_authority_set, freeze_authority_set, transfer_fee, mint_close_authority, unknown_extension, scaled_ui_amount, interest_bearing, confidential_transfer, transfer_hook_authority (a transfer hook authority is set but no hook program yet), permissioned_burn, non_transferable. `safe` has no reasons. The verdict is the highest level matched. Every figure is read at finalized commitment, so it can lag the tip of the chain by about 13 seconds; `meta.slot` is the lowest context slot of the reads behind the answer. It returns no holders, liquidity, price or metadata: `metadata_address` only names where the metadata lives.

When to use: Before accepting or swapping into an unfamiliar token, to see whether its mint can freeze, mint more, move or tax balances.

When not to use: Not a price, liquidity or holder lookup and not an audit of the token's project; it reads only the mint account.

get.summary: Whether Solana data is currently being served: latest probe status and finalized slot.
get.description:

When to use: Before relying on the Solana verdict endpoints, or to explain a 503 from them.

When not to use: Not a measure of the Solana network itself, only of this service's access to it; use the latest-slot endpoint to see chain progress.

get.summary: Can this Solana account pay the fees of N transactions now?
get.description:
Checks on finalized state whether `address` can pay the base fees of `transaction_count` transactions of `signatures` signatures each, at 5,000 lamports per signature, under the validator's fee-payer rules. `account_kind` is `none` (no account or 0 lamports), `system` (a System wallet), `nonce` (an initialized System nonce account) or `other` (it cannot pay fees, an uninitialized nonce account included). After the fees a System wallet must hold 0 or at least the live rent-exempt minimum for 0 bytes, and a nonce account at least the live rent-exempt minimum for 80 bytes. `verdict` is `not_ready` when any reason matched, else `ready`; `unknown` is not served, since a failed read fails the whole request. Reasons: account_not_found, not_fee_payer, insufficient_sol_for_fees. Warning: nonce_account. `required_fee_sol` is the total base fee in SOL; priority fees are excluded. `rent_exempt_minimum_sol` is the live rent-exempt minimum the rule compares, in SOL (for 0 bytes on `system`, for 80 bytes on `nonce`): a network figure, not the holder's; null for `none` and `other`, whose rule compares no minimum. No balance is returned. The body echoes the queried `address` and the inputs `transaction_count` and `signatures` (1 and 1 when absent). Every figure is read at finalized commitment, so it can lag the tip of the chain by about 13 seconds; `meta.slot` is the lowest context slot of the reads behind the answer.

When to use: Before sending one or more transactions from a wallet: to learn whether it can pay their base fees without dropping below its rent-exempt minimum.

When not to use: To check one SOL or token transfer end to end (use `/v1/solana/transfer-readiness`), or to read a balance (none is returned).

get.summary: Which of this wallet's Solana token accounts can be closed for rent, or are delegated or frozen?
get.description:
Scans on finalized state the SPL Token and Token-2022 accounts owned by `address`, one page of at most 1,000 accounts per program, and returns counts only: no accounts, mints, amounts or balances. Its only address is `address`, the echo of the queried owner. An account is closable when its amount is 0, its close authority (or else its owner) is `address`, and it holds no withheld transfer fee and no confidential balance; a frozen empty account is still closable. `reclaimable_rent_sol` is the lamports of the closable accounts, in SOL. `close_blocked` counts the empty accounts that cannot be closed now, by cause: withheld_transfer_fees, confidential_balance, foreign_close_authority. Verdict: risk (delegated or frozen accounts), else action_available (closable accounts), else clean. Reasons: active_token_delegates, frozen_token_accounts, reclaimable_rent, close_blocked, scan_truncated (a program had more accounts than one page). Every figure is read at finalized commitment, so it can lag the tip of the chain by about 13 seconds; `meta.slot` is the lowest context slot of the reads behind the answer.

When to use: Before cleaning up a wallet: to learn how much rent closing its empty token accounts returns, and whether any token account has an active delegate or is frozen.

When not to use: To list token accounts, mints or balances (none are returned), or to check one transfer end to end (use `/v1/solana/transfer-readiness`).

get.summary: What kind of Solana account is this address, and should a payment go to it?
get.description:
Reads the account at `address` on finalized state with one `getMultipleAccounts` call and classifies it from its owner program, executable flag and data length. `kind` is `not_found` (no account; still a 200 answer), `wallet` (System Program, 0 bytes; `on_curve` is false for a program-derived address), `nonce` (System Program, 80 bytes), `token_account` (with `token_owner`, `mint`, `token_program`, `is_ata` and `frozen`), `mint` (with `token_program`), `token_multisig`, `program` (executable), `stake`, `vote` or `other` (with `owner_program`). `frozen` is true when the token account's state is Frozen, so it refuses transfers, false when Initialized or Uninitialized, and null when the token account does not decode. Fields that do not apply to the kind are null, and `address` echoes the queried address. Payment hints: pay_token_owner (name the wallet `token_owner`, not this token account, as the recipient), not_a_payment_destination, program_owned_destination, pda_wallet. Every figure is read at finalized commitment, so it can lag the tip of the chain by about 13 seconds; `meta.slot` is the lowest context slot of the reads behind the answer.

When to use: Before sending SOL or tokens to an address: to learn whether it is a wallet, a token account (and whose), a mint, a program or another program-owned account.

When not to use: To check one transfer end to end with amounts and fees (use `/v1/solana/transfer-readiness`), or to read balances (none are returned).

get.summary: Is this Solana mint the canonical stablecoin it claims to be?
get.description:
Answers from a closed registry of canonical stablecoins, each entry taken from the issuer's own documentation. The body opens with the queried `mint`, on every answer. `canonical` is true only for a registry mint, and `registry_entry` then names the issuer and links its own documentation. `posture` is the mint's controls read live (`token_program`, `mint_authority_set`, `freeze_authority_set` and `extensions`) and compared with a dated snapshot: `posture_matches_registry` says whether every fact still matches, and `posture_differences` lists each one that changed as `<field>_changed` (the extension names are compared as a set, so their order never counts). Right after `posture`, `mint_authority` and `freeze_authority` are the mint's current mint and freeze authority addresses, decoded from the same mint read, each `null` when the mint has none: live facts, never compared with the snapshot and never in `posture_differences`. A registry mint that no longer decodes answers `posture: null` with `mint_not_found`, still 200, and with both authorities `null`; a mint outside the registry has both `null` too. The registry never changes the token verdict: the PYUSD mint of the example keeps its own `danger` verdict with `permanent_delegate` on `/v1/solana/token/{mint}` while its stablecoin answer is canonical, so read both before accepting a token. No regulatory or licensing status is returned, and a canonical answer is not an endorsement of the token. Every figure is read at finalized commitment, so it can lag the tip of the chain by about 13 seconds; `meta.slot` is the lowest context slot of the reads behind the answer.

When to use: Before accepting or quoting a stablecoin: to check the mint is the canonical one and that its mint facts have not changed since the snapshot.

When not to use: To read supply or balances (use `/v1/solana/token/{mint}`), or as a regulatory or licensing check: none is served.

get.summary: Did this settled Solana payment deliver the expected amount to the expected recipient?
get.description:
Reads the transaction `signature` once at `finalized` and compares what the recipient received with what you expected, returning a derived `verdict` and nothing else about the accounts. The answer is never an error when the transaction is absent: `not_found` (the node served no transaction, and the signature has no status or a `finalized` one) and `not_final` (it is not finalized yet) are verdicts with a 200, and neither is definitive: ask again later. The other verdicts are `failed` (the transaction errored), `unverifiable` (a token balance entry for the mint names no owner, so who received it cannot be told), `reference_mismatch` (only with `reference`), `wrong_sender` (only with `source`), `paid`, `underpaid`, `wrong_asset` (the recipient's balance rose in another mint or in SOL) and `wrong_recipient`. The first verdict that matches, in that order, is the one returned.

| Verdict | What settles it | Definitive |
|---|---|---|
| `not_found` | the node served no transaction, and the signature has no status or a `finalized` one | not definitive: ask again later |
| `not_final` | the transaction is not finalized yet | not definitive: ask again later |
| `failed` | the transaction errored | definitive |
| `unverifiable` | a token balance entry for the mint names no owner, so who received it cannot be told | definitive |
| `reference_mismatch` | `reference` is given and is not among the account keys | definitive |
| `wrong_sender` | `source` is given and did not sign the transaction | definitive |
| `paid` | the recipient received at least `amount` | definitive |
| `underpaid` | the recipient received more than 0 and less than `amount` | definitive |
| `wrong_asset` | the recipient's balance rose in another mint or in SOL | definitive |
| `wrong_recipient` | none of the above applies | definitive |

`failure_code` is the error variant name of a failed transaction's `meta.err` (the string, or the single key of a one-key object), such as `InstructionError`, never the error object itself; an error of any other shape, or a name that does not match `^[A-Za-z0-9_]{1,40}$`, is reported as `unknown_error`. It is `null` when the transaction did not fail and when there is no transaction. `expected`, `delivered` and `excess` are amount objects `{asset, value, value_atomic}`: `asset` is the `mint` you passed (or `SOL`), `value` the amount in SOL or token units and `value_atomic` the same amount in lamports or raw base units, both exact; `expected.value` is your `amount` as its canonical exact decimal (`1.50` is `1.5`). `delivered` is what the recipient's own balance gained, so a Token-2022 transfer fee is already deducted and a token account closed in the same transaction counts its whole balance as a negative delta. `excess` is what was delivered above `amount` on a `paid` verdict, and `null` otherwise. When the mint does not appear in the transaction's token balances its decimals are unknown and nothing is guessed: `expected.value_atomic` and `delivered.value` are then `null`. `settled_at` is the block time of the slot holding the transaction (`slot`), `null` when the node reports none; with no transaction to read, `delivered`, `excess`, `slot` and `settled_at` are `null`. After `valuation` the body echoes the queried `signature`, `recipient`, `reference` and `source`, in that order; `reference` and `source` are `null` when the request did not send them. `valuation` is an informative EUR and USD reference value given only on a `paid` or `underpaid` verdict for a registry stablecoin when an ECB rate on or before the payment date is stored; otherwise it is `null`. The value is an informative reference, not a tax figure. Source: ECB statistics. A finalized transaction never changes, so its answer is fresh for 86400 seconds and served stale for up to 604800; `not_found` and `not_final` are fresh for 4 seconds and served stale for up to 30. If the upstream read fails, an answer cached within its stale window is served instead of a 503. Every figure is read at finalized commitment, so it can lag the tip of the chain by about 13 seconds; `meta.slot` is the lowest context slot of the reads behind the answer.

When to use: After a payment has been submitted: to confirm from the chain that the recipient received the mint and amount you expected, including the Token-2022 fee case.

When not to use: Before sending a transfer (use `/v1/solana/transfer-readiness`), or to list a wallet's transfers or balances (none are returned).

get.summary: Can this payer settle this x402 payment requirement right now?
get.description:
Takes one x402 v2 `exact` requirement as an SVM server states it (`asset`, the mint the payment moves, `amount` in that mint's base units and `pay_to`) plus the `payer` wallet, and answers one `verdict`: `block` on any blocker, `warn` with warnings only, else `ok`. The facilitator is the fee payer (`extra.feePayer`) and pays only the network fee, so `insufficient_sol_for_fees` and `source_below_rent_exempt` never apply here (the embedded `readiness` may still list them). A `pay_to` without a token account for the mint is the blocker `pay_to_ata_missing`: the payment is a `TransferChecked` to the existing associated token account of `pay_to` and `asset`, and the fee payer may not appear in any instruction, so nothing in that transaction can create it; an address already occupied by another program's account is the different blocker `destination_ata_occupied`, carried as it is. `readiness` is what `/v1/solana/transfer-readiness` answers for the same payer, recipient, mint and amount, without its `meta`, so both routes can be compared field by field; its `amount` is the UI rendering of the atomic `amount` once the mint's decimals are read. Each readiness reason becomes the blocker `payer_<code>` and each readiness warning the warning `payer_<code>`. When the embedded `readiness` lists a failed check (`checks_failed` not empty: the payer's or `pay_to`'s token account cannot be decoded), the warning `payer_readiness_unknown` is added, whatever its reasons, so such a payment is never a bare `ok`. A `pay_to` that is a token account, mint, multisig, program, stake or vote account is the blocker `pay_to_not_wallet`, and one owned by another program the warning `pay_to_program_owned`; `destination_not_wallet`, `destination_program_owned` and `destination_ata_occupied` are then not repeated as `payer_*`, while the embedded `readiness` still lists them. An off-curve wallet and an address with no account are not `pay_to_not_wallet`; whether either has the token account is the separate `pay_to_ata_missing` check. An `asset` that is not the canonical stablecoin of the registry gives the warning `asset_not_canonical`. `pay_to` must differ from `payer`: the same address is a 400 naming `pay_to`, and nothing is read. `pay_to` is read in the same batch as the readiness accounts, so the check makes exactly the readiness reads and no others.

| Code | What it states | Blocks or warns |
|---|---|---|
| `pay_to_not_wallet` | `pay_to` is a token account, mint, multisig, program, stake or vote account | blocks |
| `pay_to_ata_missing` | `pay_to` has no token account for the mint, and nothing in the transaction can create it | blocks |
| `destination_ata_occupied` | the address of the associated token account is already occupied by another program's account | blocks |
| `pay_to_program_owned` | `pay_to` is owned by another program | warns |
| `asset_not_canonical` | `asset` is not the canonical stablecoin of the registry | warns |
| `payer_readiness_unknown` | the embedded `readiness` lists a failed check: the payer's or `pay_to`'s token account cannot be decoded | warns |
| `payer_*` | every applicable payer readiness reason appears with the prefix `payer_` (`payer_<code>`), and each readiness warning appears as the warning `payer_<code>`; the codes are those of `/v1/solana/transfer-readiness` | blocks or warns, as the readiness code does |

Every figure is read at finalized commitment, so it can lag the tip of the chain by about 13 seconds; `meta.slot` is the lowest context slot of the reads behind the answer.

When to use: After an x402 server answered 402 with a Solana `exact` requirement: to check, before signing, that this payer can settle that exact requirement to that recipient now.

When not to use: For a transfer that is not an x402 requirement (use `/v1/solana/transfer-readiness`), or once the payment has settled (use `/v1/solana/payment/verify`).

get.summary: Will this Solana transfer succeed? A verdict for SOL or an SPL or Token-2022 token.
get.description:
Checks one planned transfer of SOL or of an SPL Token or Token-2022 token against finalized on-chain state and returns a `verdict` (`ready`, `not_ready` or `unknown`), every matched reason (blocking code) and warning code, `checks_failed`, and the derived figures: the amount in base units (`amount_atomic`), the source's balance of the asset that insufficient_balance compares (`source_balance`, `{asset, value, value_atomic}` in display and base units: the source token account's amount, or the source's lamports for SOL; zero when the source has no token account of the mint; for a source token account that cannot be decoded, its base-layout amount, or null without the 165-byte base), the token accounts the transfer debits and credits (`source_token_account` and `destination_token_account`, the derived associated token accounts, the destination's also when it must be created or another program's account holds its address; null for SOL), whether the destination token account must be created and the lamports to create it (its rent, or only the shortfall when its address already holds SOL), the Token-2022 transfer fee and the net amount in base units (`transfer_fee_atomic`, `net_amount_atomic`), plus `destination_kind` (the class of the destination account), the display fields `ui_multiplier` and `interest_rate_pct` (percent) of mints that scale their UI amount, and `transfer_fee_next` when a newer transfer fee is pending (its `transfer_fee_pct`, its `transfer_fee_max` in display units and its `epoch`). Reasons: insufficient_balance, insufficient_sol_for_fees (5,000 lamports for one signature, priority fees excluded, plus the lamports to create the destination token account when it is missing, only the shortfall when its address already holds SOL, plus the amount for SOL), source_below_rent_exempt, destination_below_rent_exempt, source_frozen, destination_frozen, non_transferable, mint_paused, destination_ata_occupied (an account owned by another program already holds the destination's token account address, so the token account cannot be created there), destination_frozen_on_creation (the mint's default account state would create the destination token account frozen), destination_not_wallet (the destination is a token account, mint, multisig, program, stake or vote account: pay its owner wallet), destination_ata_owner_mismatch (the account at the destination's token account address belongs to another owner), source_not_system_account (a SOL transfer from an account that is not a plain System wallet, such as a nonce account), destination_confidential_only (the destination token account refuses non-confidential credits). Warnings: destination_off_curve, memo_required, destination_program_owned (the destination is an account of kind `other`: owned by another program, or a System account with unexpected data), ui_amount_scaled (the mint scales its UI amount; `amount` stays raw / 10^decimals, and `ui_multiplier` and `interest_rate_pct` are for display only), transfer_fee_changing (a newer transfer fee starts at a later epoch; see `transfer_fee_next`). `verdict` is `not_ready` on any reason, else `unknown` on any failed check, else `ready`. `checks_failed` names source_token_account or destination_token_account when that token account exists but cannot be decoded (an SPL Token account of a length other than 165 bytes, a Token-2022 account under 165 bytes, a Token-2022 account of the multisig length of 355 bytes, a Token-2022 account type byte other than 2, a bad TLV, a ConfidentialTransferAccount of a size other than 295 bytes, or an account state byte other than 0 (uninitialized), 1 (initialized) or 2 (frozen)): its memo and confidential-credit state is then unknown, never read as absent, and an undecodable destination token account is never reported as missing; an undecodable source still gives insufficient_balance when the amount in its base layout is below the transfer amount. Any other failed read fails the whole request. The rent-exempt minimum is read live and never hardcoded. Every figure is read at finalized commitment, so it can lag the tip of the chain by about 13 seconds; `meta.slot` is the lowest context slot of the reads behind the answer. The amount is not part of any cache key, so the verdict is computed per request.

When to use: Before building or signing a Solana transfer, to learn whether it will fail and what it will cost in rent and fees.

When not to use: Not a simulation of the exact transaction (no priority fee, no program logic), not a token price or holder lookup, and not a way to read raw accounts. Per call: 0.0242 EUR at the default regime. With prepaid credits, debit per call: 0.02 EUR-denominated units (approx 50 calls per bundle) or 0.024 USD-denominated units (approx 34 calls per bundle).

get.summary: Is this Solana token safe to hold or receive? A safe, warn or danger verdict.
get.description:
Decodes an SPL Token or Token-2022 mint (including its extensions) and returns the token program, decimals, the exact supply in base units (`supply_atomic`) and in display units (`supply`, `supply_atomic` / 10^decimals, exact, not adjusted by a UI multiplier or interest rate), the authorities, the extension names, the transfer fee active at the current epoch (`transfer_fee_pct` in percent and `transfer_fee_max`, the maximum fee per transfer in display units of the mint, exact; both null without a TransferFeeConfig), the values of the extensions it decodes, each null without its extension (`transfer_fee_next`, the newer fee while its epoch is after the current epoch, with its `transfer_fee_pct`, its `transfer_fee_max` in display units and its `epoch`; `transfer_fee_authority`; `paused`; `default_account_state`, `initialized` or `frozen`; `interest_rate_pct`, an annual rate in percent compounded continuously; `ui_multiplier`, the ScaledUiAmount multiplier in effect; `ui_multiplier_next` and `ui_multiplier_next_at`, the new multiplier and its effective time while that time is after the response time (`ui_multiplier_next` null when the new multiplier is not a finite number, its time still served); `permanent_delegate`; `transfer_hook_program_id`; `mint_close_authority`; `metadata_address`; a key that is unset is null) and a `verdict` (`safe`, `warn` or `danger`) with every matched reason code. `danger`: permanent_delegate, transfer_hook, pausable, default_account_frozen. `warn`: mint_authority_set, freeze_authority_set, transfer_fee, mint_close_authority, unknown_extension, scaled_ui_amount, interest_bearing, confidential_transfer, transfer_hook_authority (a transfer hook authority is set but no hook program yet), permissioned_burn, non_transferable. `safe` has no reasons. The verdict is the highest level matched. Every figure is read at finalized commitment, so it can lag the tip of the chain by about 13 seconds; `meta.slot` is the lowest context slot of the reads behind the answer. It returns no holders, liquidity, price or metadata: `metadata_address` only names where the metadata lives.

When to use: Before accepting or swapping into an unfamiliar token, to see whether its mint can freeze, mint more, move or tax balances.

When not to use: Not a price, liquidity or holder lookup and not an audit of the token's project; it reads only the mint account. Per call: 0.0121 EUR at the default regime. With prepaid credits, debit per call: 0.0025 EUR-denominated units (approx 400 calls per bundle) or 0.003 USD-denominated units (approx 273 calls per bundle).

get.summary: Latest finalized Solana slot and its block time.
get.description:
Returns the latest finalized slot and the time of its block (null when the node does not have it yet). Every figure is read at finalized commitment, so it can lag the tip of the chain by about 13 seconds; `meta.slot` is the lowest context slot of the reads behind the answer.

When to use: To check how fresh the finalized view of Solana is, or to anchor a read to a slot.

When not to use: Not a tip-of-chain feed: it is finalized, not processed or confirmed, and it is cached for 2 seconds. Per call: 0.0121 EUR at the default regime. With prepaid credits, debit per call: 0.0005 EUR-denominated units (approx 2000 calls per bundle) or 0.0006 USD-denominated units (approx 1366 calls per bundle).

get.summary: Whether Solana data is currently being served: latest probe status and finalized slot.
get.description:
Reports the result of the latest stored probe (`up`, `down`, `unknown`) with its finalized slot and latency, without calling Solana. The status is `unavailable` while Solana data is not configured on this service, and `unknown` before the first probe is stored. `meta.slot` is the slot of the latest probe sample when that sample is up, and null, never 0, when there is no finalized slot to report (Solana data not configured, no probe stored yet, or the latest sample down or without a slot); `slot` is null in the same cases. It does not name the upstream provider.

When to use: Before relying on the Solana verdict endpoints, or to explain a 503 from them.

When not to use: Not a measure of the Solana network itself, only of this service's access to it; use the latest-slot endpoint to see chain progress. Per call: 0.0121 EUR at the default regime. With prepaid credits, debit per call: 0.0005 EUR-denominated units (approx 2000 calls per bundle) or 0.0006 USD-denominated units (approx 1366 calls per bundle).

get.summary: Bucketed history of Solana probe results over 1 hour, 24 hours or 7 days.
get.description:
Aggregates the stored probes into time buckets with sample count, successful samples, uptime percentage (`uptime_pct`, up / samples x 100 as a decimal string rounded half-up to 2 places) and average latency. It returns whatever samples are stored, even while Solana data is not configured, and never names the upstream provider. `meta.slot` is the highest slot of the window's up samples, and null, never 0, when no up sample in the window carries one.

When to use: To see whether Solana data was reliable over the last hour, day or week.

When not to use: Not a record of chain activity; it describes this service's access to Solana. Per call: 0.0121 EUR at the default regime. With prepaid credits, debit per call: 0.0005 EUR-denominated units (approx 2000 calls per bundle) or 0.0006 USD-denominated units (approx 1366 calls per bundle).

get.summary: Can this Solana account pay the fees of N transactions now?
get.description:
Checks on finalized state whether `address` can pay the base fees of `transaction_count` transactions of `signatures` signatures each, at 5,000 lamports per signature, under the validator's fee-payer rules. `account_kind` is `none` (no account or 0 lamports), `system` (a System wallet), `nonce` (an initialized System nonce account) or `other` (it cannot pay fees, an uninitialized nonce account included). After the fees a System wallet must hold 0 or at least the live rent-exempt minimum for 0 bytes, and a nonce account at least the live rent-exempt minimum for 80 bytes. `verdict` is `not_ready` when any reason matched, else `ready`; `unknown` is not served, since a failed read fails the whole request. Reasons: account_not_found, not_fee_payer, insufficient_sol_for_fees. Warning: nonce_account. `required_fee_sol` is the total base fee in SOL; priority fees are excluded. `rent_exempt_minimum_sol` is the live rent-exempt minimum the rule compares, in SOL (for 0 bytes on `system`, for 80 bytes on `nonce`): a network figure, not the holder's; null for `none` and `other`, whose rule compares no minimum. No balance is returned. The body echoes the queried `address` and the inputs `transaction_count` and `signatures` (1 and 1 when absent). Every figure is read at finalized commitment, so it can lag the tip of the chain by about 13 seconds; `meta.slot` is the lowest context slot of the reads behind the answer.

When to use: Before sending one or more transactions from a wallet: to learn whether it can pay their base fees without dropping below its rent-exempt minimum.

When not to use: To check one SOL or token transfer end to end (use `/v1/solana/transfer-readiness`), or to read a balance (none is returned). Per call: 0.0121 EUR at the default regime. With prepaid credits, debit per call: 0.0025 EUR-denominated units (approx 400 calls per bundle) or 0.003 USD-denominated units (approx 273 calls per bundle).

get.summary: Which of this wallet's Solana token accounts can be closed for rent, or are delegated or frozen?
get.description:
Scans on finalized state the SPL Token and Token-2022 accounts owned by `address`, one page of at most 1,000 accounts per program, and returns counts only: no accounts, mints, amounts or balances. Its only address is `address`, the echo of the queried owner. An account is closable when its amount is 0, its close authority (or else its owner) is `address`, and it holds no withheld transfer fee and no confidential balance; a frozen empty account is still closable. `reclaimable_rent_sol` is the lamports of the closable accounts, in SOL. `close_blocked` counts the empty accounts that cannot be closed now, by cause: withheld_transfer_fees, confidential_balance, foreign_close_authority. Verdict: risk (delegated or frozen accounts), else action_available (closable accounts), else clean. Reasons: active_token_delegates, frozen_token_accounts, reclaimable_rent, close_blocked, scan_truncated (a program had more accounts than one page). Every figure is read at finalized commitment, so it can lag the tip of the chain by about 13 seconds; `meta.slot` is the lowest context slot of the reads behind the answer.

When to use: Before cleaning up a wallet: to learn how much rent closing its empty token accounts returns, and whether any token account has an active delegate or is frozen.

When not to use: To list token accounts, mints or balances (none are returned), or to check one transfer end to end (use `/v1/solana/transfer-readiness`). Per call: 0.0121 EUR at the default regime. With prepaid credits, debit per call: 0.0025 EUR-denominated units (approx 400 calls per bundle) or 0.003 USD-denominated units (approx 273 calls per bundle).
