get.summary: What kind of Solana account is this address, and should a payment go to it?
get.description:
Reads the account at `address` on finalized state with one `getMultipleAccounts` call and classifies it from its owner program, executable flag and data length. `kind` is `not_found` (no account; still a 200 answer), `wallet` (System Program, 0 bytes; `on_curve` is false for a program-derived address), `nonce` (System Program, 80 bytes), `token_account` (with `token_owner`, `mint`, `token_program`, `is_ata` and `frozen`), `mint` (with `token_program`), `token_multisig`, `program` (executable), `stake`, `vote` or `other` (with `owner_program`). `frozen` is true when the token account's state is Frozen, so it refuses transfers, false when Initialized or Uninitialized, and null when the token account does not decode. Fields that do not apply to the kind are null, and `address` echoes the queried address. Payment hints: pay_token_owner (name the wallet `token_owner`, not this token account, as the recipient), not_a_payment_destination, program_owned_destination, pda_wallet. Every figure is read at finalized commitment, so it can lag the tip of the chain by about 13 seconds; `meta.slot` is the lowest context slot of the reads behind the answer.

When to use: Before sending SOL or tokens to an address: to learn whether it is a wallet, a token account (and whose), a mint, a program or another program-owned account.

When not to use: To check one transfer end to end with amounts and fees (use `/v1/solana/transfer-readiness`), or to read balances (none are returned). Per call: 0.0121 EUR at the default regime. With prepaid credits, debit per call: 0.0005 EUR-denominated units (approx 2000 calls per bundle) or 0.0006 USD-denominated units (approx 1366 calls per bundle).

get.summary: Is this Solana mint the canonical stablecoin it claims to be?
get.description:
Answers from a closed registry of canonical stablecoins, each entry taken from the issuer's own documentation. The body opens with the queried `mint`, on every answer. `canonical` is true only for a registry mint, and `registry_entry` then names the issuer and links its own documentation. `posture` is the mint's controls read live (`token_program`, `mint_authority_set`, `freeze_authority_set` and `extensions`) and compared with a dated snapshot: `posture_matches_registry` says whether every fact still matches, and `posture_differences` lists each one that changed as `<field>_changed` (the extension names are compared as a set, so their order never counts). Right after `posture`, `mint_authority` and `freeze_authority` are the mint's current mint and freeze authority addresses, decoded from the same mint read, each `null` when the mint has none: live facts, never compared with the snapshot and never in `posture_differences`. A registry mint that no longer decodes answers `posture: null` with `mint_not_found`, still 200, and with both authorities `null`; a mint outside the registry has both `null` too. The registry never changes the token verdict: the PYUSD mint of the example keeps its own `danger` verdict with `permanent_delegate` on `/v1/solana/token/{mint}` while its stablecoin answer is canonical, so read both before accepting a token. No regulatory or licensing status is returned, and a canonical answer is not an endorsement of the token. Every figure is read at finalized commitment, so it can lag the tip of the chain by about 13 seconds; `meta.slot` is the lowest context slot of the reads behind the answer.

When to use: Before accepting or quoting a stablecoin: to check the mint is the canonical one and that its mint facts have not changed since the snapshot.

When not to use: To read supply or balances (use `/v1/solana/token/{mint}`), or as a regulatory or licensing check: none is served. Per call: 0.0121 EUR at the default regime. With prepaid credits, debit per call: 0.0005 EUR-denominated units (approx 2000 calls per bundle) or 0.0006 USD-denominated units (approx 1366 calls per bundle).

get.summary: Did this settled Solana payment deliver the expected amount to the expected recipient?
get.description:
Reads the transaction `signature` once at `finalized` and compares what the recipient received with what you expected, returning a derived `verdict` and nothing else about the accounts. The answer is never an error when the transaction is absent: `not_found` (the node served no transaction, and the signature has no status or a `finalized` one) and `not_final` (it is not finalized yet) are verdicts with a 200, and neither is definitive: ask again later. The other verdicts are `failed` (the transaction errored), `unverifiable` (a token balance entry for the mint names no owner, so who received it cannot be told), `reference_mismatch` (only with `reference`), `wrong_sender` (only with `source`), `paid`, `underpaid`, `wrong_asset` (the recipient's balance rose in another mint or in SOL) and `wrong_recipient`. The first verdict that matches, in that order, is the one returned.

| Verdict | What settles it | Definitive |
|---|---|---|
| `not_found` | the node served no transaction, and the signature has no status or a `finalized` one | not definitive: ask again later |
| `not_final` | the transaction is not finalized yet | not definitive: ask again later |
| `failed` | the transaction errored | definitive |
| `unverifiable` | a token balance entry for the mint names no owner, so who received it cannot be told | definitive |
| `reference_mismatch` | `reference` is given and is not among the account keys | definitive |
| `wrong_sender` | `source` is given and did not sign the transaction | definitive |
| `paid` | the recipient received at least `amount` | definitive |
| `underpaid` | the recipient received more than 0 and less than `amount` | definitive |
| `wrong_asset` | the recipient's balance rose in another mint or in SOL | definitive |
| `wrong_recipient` | none of the above applies | definitive |

`failure_code` is the error variant name of a failed transaction's `meta.err` (the string, or the single key of a one-key object), such as `InstructionError`, never the error object itself; an error of any other shape, or a name that does not match `^[A-Za-z0-9_]{1,40}$`, is reported as `unknown_error`. It is `null` when the transaction did not fail and when there is no transaction. `expected`, `delivered` and `excess` are amount objects `{asset, value, value_atomic}`: `asset` is the `mint` you passed (or `SOL`), `value` the amount in SOL or token units and `value_atomic` the same amount in lamports or raw base units, both exact; `expected.value` is your `amount` as its canonical exact decimal (`1.50` is `1.5`). `delivered` is what the recipient's own balance gained, so a Token-2022 transfer fee is already deducted and a token account closed in the same transaction counts its whole balance as a negative delta. `excess` is what was delivered above `amount` on a `paid` verdict, and `null` otherwise. When the mint does not appear in the transaction's token balances its decimals are unknown and nothing is guessed: `expected.value_atomic` and `delivered.value` are then `null`. `settled_at` is the block time of the slot holding the transaction (`slot`), `null` when the node reports none; with no transaction to read, `delivered`, `excess`, `slot` and `settled_at` are `null`. After `valuation` the body echoes the queried `signature`, `recipient`, `reference` and `source`, in that order; `reference` and `source` are `null` when the request did not send them. `valuation` is an informative EUR and USD reference value given only on a `paid` or `underpaid` verdict for a registry stablecoin when an ECB rate on or before the payment date is stored; otherwise it is `null`. The value is an informative reference, not a tax figure. Source: ECB statistics. A finalized transaction never changes, so its answer is fresh for 86400 seconds and served stale for up to 604800; `not_found` and `not_final` are fresh for 4 seconds and served stale for up to 30. If the upstream read fails, an answer cached within its stale window is served instead of a 503. Every figure is read at finalized commitment, so it can lag the tip of the chain by about 13 seconds; `meta.slot` is the lowest context slot of the reads behind the answer.

When to use: After a payment has been submitted: to confirm from the chain that the recipient received the mint and amount you expected, including the Token-2022 fee case.

When not to use: Before sending a transfer (use `/v1/solana/transfer-readiness`), or to list a wallet's transfers or balances (none are returned). Per call: 0.0121 EUR at the default regime. With prepaid credits, debit per call: 0.0025 EUR-denominated units (approx 400 calls per bundle) or 0.003 USD-denominated units (approx 273 calls per bundle).

get.summary: Can this payer settle this x402 payment requirement right now?
get.description:
Takes one x402 v2 `exact` requirement as an SVM server states it (`asset`, the mint the payment moves, `amount` in that mint's base units and `pay_to`) plus the `payer` wallet, and answers one `verdict`: `block` on any blocker, `warn` with warnings only, else `ok`. The facilitator is the fee payer (`extra.feePayer`) and pays only the network fee, so `insufficient_sol_for_fees` and `source_below_rent_exempt` never apply here (the embedded `readiness` may still list them). A `pay_to` without a token account for the mint is the blocker `pay_to_ata_missing`: the payment is a `TransferChecked` to the existing associated token account of `pay_to` and `asset`, and the fee payer may not appear in any instruction, so nothing in that transaction can create it; an address already occupied by another program's account is the different blocker `destination_ata_occupied`, carried as it is. `readiness` is what `/v1/solana/transfer-readiness` answers for the same payer, recipient, mint and amount, without its `meta`, so both routes can be compared field by field; its `amount` is the UI rendering of the atomic `amount` once the mint's decimals are read. Each readiness reason becomes the blocker `payer_<code>` and each readiness warning the warning `payer_<code>`. When the embedded `readiness` lists a failed check (`checks_failed` not empty: the payer's or `pay_to`'s token account cannot be decoded), the warning `payer_readiness_unknown` is added, whatever its reasons, so such a payment is never a bare `ok`. A `pay_to` that is a token account, mint, multisig, program, stake or vote account is the blocker `pay_to_not_wallet`, and one owned by another program the warning `pay_to_program_owned`; `destination_not_wallet`, `destination_program_owned` and `destination_ata_occupied` are then not repeated as `payer_*`, while the embedded `readiness` still lists them. An off-curve wallet and an address with no account are not `pay_to_not_wallet`; whether either has the token account is the separate `pay_to_ata_missing` check. An `asset` that is not the canonical stablecoin of the registry gives the warning `asset_not_canonical`. `pay_to` must differ from `payer`: the same address is a 400 naming `pay_to`, and nothing is read. `pay_to` is read in the same batch as the readiness accounts, so the check makes exactly the readiness reads and no others.

| Code | What it states | Blocks or warns |
|---|---|---|
| `pay_to_not_wallet` | `pay_to` is a token account, mint, multisig, program, stake or vote account | blocks |
| `pay_to_ata_missing` | `pay_to` has no token account for the mint, and nothing in the transaction can create it | blocks |
| `destination_ata_occupied` | the address of the associated token account is already occupied by another program's account | blocks |
| `pay_to_program_owned` | `pay_to` is owned by another program | warns |
| `asset_not_canonical` | `asset` is not the canonical stablecoin of the registry | warns |
| `payer_readiness_unknown` | the embedded `readiness` lists a failed check: the payer's or `pay_to`'s token account cannot be decoded | warns |
| `payer_*` | every applicable payer readiness reason appears with the prefix `payer_` (`payer_<code>`), and each readiness warning appears as the warning `payer_<code>`; the codes are those of `/v1/solana/transfer-readiness` | blocks or warns, as the readiness code does |

Every figure is read at finalized commitment, so it can lag the tip of the chain by about 13 seconds; `meta.slot` is the lowest context slot of the reads behind the answer.

When to use: After an x402 server answered 402 with a Solana `exact` requirement: to check, before signing, that this payer can settle that exact requirement to that recipient now.

When not to use: For a transfer that is not an x402 requirement (use `/v1/solana/transfer-readiness`), or once the payment has settled (use `/v1/solana/payment/verify`). Per call: 0.0242 EUR at the default regime. With prepaid credits, debit per call: 0.02 EUR-denominated units (approx 50 calls per bundle) or 0.024 USD-denominated units (approx 34 calls per bundle).

Without it the route answers 402 with the accepted payment options, but only while paid access is active; while payments are off the route returns free data with or without the header. One payment covers exactly one call.

parameters.description: Base64 of the JSON x402 v2 payment payload, at most 8192 bytes. Without it the route answers 402 with the accepted payment options, but only while paid access is active; while payments are off the route returns free data with or without the header. One payment covers exactly one call. The payment payload key depends on the rail of the chosen `accepts` entry: `payload.transaction` (base64 signed transaction) on Solana; `payload.signedTxBlob` (hex signed transaction) and an optional `payload.invoiceId` on the XRP Ledger. See /docs/guides/payments.md.

retry_after_seconds.description: Seconds to wait before retrying, the same value as the `Retry-After` header, on every problem sent with that header (such as 429 `rate-limited` and 503 `upstream-unavailable`), so a client that cannot read headers, like an MCP tool result, still gets the delay. 402.description: Payment Required (only while paid access is active; while payments are off the route returns free data): no payment, or a payment that was not accepted (`payment-required`), a settlement that failed (`payment-settlement-failed`) or a payment that was already used for another request, or whose redelivery window or limit has passed (`payment-already-used`). Nothing is served and nothing is kept for the caller; sign a new payment from the options in `PAYMENT-REQUIRED`.

PAYMENT-REQUIRED.description: Base64 of the JSON `PaymentRequired` object (see the `PaymentRequired` schema) with the accepted payment options. Sent on 402 answers that can be fixed by paying.
